That said, the inter-State distribution of Lok Sabha seats is such a central question of democracy and federalism that any changes must be preceded by thoughtful deliberations at multiple levels.
• That makes the approach of the Centre , which is trying to pass a constitutional amendment through defections and manipulations, dubious and lacking in good faith. If the Centre has been willing to extend the constitutional guarantee of inter-State distribution of seats on the basis of the 1971 Census, it could have built an all-party consensus on the issue . Instead, in April, it made a deceptive move by promising to maintain the current proportion of seats while the constitutional amendment it moved would have made that promise unconstitutional. At present, when the Centre is keen to appear accommodative, a more appropriate manner to proceed with such a generational measure in India’s federal democracy is to refer the Bills to a parliamentary committee that can examine them in detail and generate a national conversation. A bigger Lok Sabha will create its own challenges , while the case for increasing its size is not entirely without merit as India’s population has grown by at least 2.6 times since the 1971 Census, which forms the basis of the last delimitation of 1973, based on the 1971 Census. The Centre should not rush this vital question, which is not merely about garnering enough votes for passing a Bill. It must be based on consensus, as it happened in 1976 and again in 2001, under a Prime Minister from the Congress and one from the BJP, respectively.

articles.title: Cultural values of language remain irreplaceable in AI era: Arabic meet
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Artificial Intelligence (AI) may transform the way Arabic is learned and used, but human emotions and traditional values remain beyond the reach of technology, an international conference on the Arabic language held at Anvarul Islam Arabic College, Kuniyil, observed on Thursday.

The two-day conference, titled ‘Digital humanities: reimagining Arabic language and literature’, was organised by the Arabic department of the college in association with Calicut University’s Arabic department, Kerala State Higher Education Council, and Arab Union of Internet Writers.
Liyaqat Ali, deputy director of collegiate education, inaugurated the conference on Wednesday. College Principal K. Mohammed Fawaz presided over the function.
Liyaqat Ali, deputy director of collegiate education, inaugurating an international conference on Arabic at Anvarul Islam Arabic College, Kuniyil, on Wednesday. | Photo Credit: SAKEER HUSSAIN

Arabic scholars Sumayya Ibrahim Abu Thailath from Palestine, Najeeb Ali Mulkhath from Yemen, Simi K. Salim, K. Ali Noufal, I.P. Abdul Salam, C.M. Sabir Navas, K.A. Nasser, P. Firoz, M.K. Ameer Swalahi, Shakir Babu Kuniyil, and K.P. Abdul Haleem Thangal spoke.
E.T. Mohammed Basheer, MP, inaugurated the valedictory function on Thursday. He highlighted the growing global significance of the Arabic language in an increasingly interconnected world.
Scholars Mujeeb Nellikkuth, Ali Jafar, Mohammed Aman K., P. Sulaiman and C. Abdul Wahab spoke.

articles.title: Accused shot during exchange of fire with police West Bengal’s Asansol
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The dramatic operation unfolded in the congested neighbourhood, with armed police personnel in plain clothes searching narrow lanes and houses, and climbing boundary walls to trace the accused

An accused wanted in multiple cases in West Bengal’s Asansol, was on Friday (November 27, 2026) shot in his right leg during an alleged clash leading to an exchange of fire with the police when they went to arrest him on Friday morning. The accused, Pratap Das, is wanted in several cases of robbery, theft, iron smuggling, and cyber fraud across Asansol. Police have been searching for him for the past few days in connection with a cyber fraud case lodged last week at Asansol South Police Station. When the police went to arrest him on Friday (November 27, 2026) from a hideout in the Ismail area, he opened fire at the police team. Later, he was shot in retaliatory fire.
According to the police, an operation to arrest Pratap was launched on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) when he again opened fire at the police team upon spotting them and managed to flee.

The operation was launched by the Asansol Durgapur Police Commissionerate Special Operations Group (SOG), along with officers from Hirapur police station, following a tip-off that he was hiding in the area and carrying a firearm. The dramatic operation unfolded in the congested neighbourhood, with armed police personnel in plain clothes searching narrow lanes and houses, and climbing boundary walls to trace the accused.

Shots of firing were heard in broad daylight causing panic among residents who witnessed a cat and mouse chase between the accused and police. The accused was seen being dragged from one of the houses out by the police with blood dripping from his right leg and was carried on all fours to a police vehicle.

Local residents in the area said that they had no idea about the accused. “We did not know that he was hiding in our neighbourhood. I went to drop my daughter off at school when I saw police chasing him. It was scary,” said a woman who stays in the area from where Pratap was arrested.

Association for Protection of Democratic Reforms, a civil rights group raised questions about the manner in which police paraded in groups with weapons. “Instead of relying on intelligence inputs, a scientific approach, and proper procedures to apprehend the criminal, the police’s actual objective was to intimidate the general public through a display of firepower,” APDR vice president Ranajit Sur said.

The development comes after a total of five encounters that took place in West Bengal since the new Bharatiya Janata Party government came to power. Five people who have been shot dead by the police during these incidents include three accused in rape cases of minors and two accused of murder.

articles.title: Not a single foot of blacktopping done on Amarnath route, PDP-BJP stoking Hindu-Muslim discord: Omar Abdullah
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: ‘The BJP and those carrying the symbol of pen and inkpot are again trying to foment Hindu-Muslim discord over the Amarnath route,’ said Omar Abdullah

J&K Chief Minister Omar Abdullah on Friday (November 27, 2026) said not a single foot of blacktopping was carried out on the Amarnath route, while referring to the Sheshnag controversy, and accused the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) of “deliberately pitting Hindus and Muslims against each other”.

“The BJP and those carrying the symbol of pen and inkpot [referring to the PDP] are again trying to foment Hindu-Muslim discord over the Amarnath route. They are alleging macadamisation. I challenge them to prove a single foot of blacktopping done on the route. I am ready to face an inquiry. There is a court [Supreme Court] direction to have a 12-feet stretch,” said Mr. Abdullah.

Mr. Abdullah’s statement came days after local parties, religious leaders, environmentalists and civil society bodies reacted sharply to the presence of an earthmover close functioning to the Sheshnag lake situation at an altitude of 11,780 feet on the way to the Amarnath shrine, which is around 20 km away from the spot.

A report prepared by the J&K Forest Department on the viral video, in which an earthmover was seen close to the lake, said, “The activity seen in the video is part of routine annual maintenance operations being undertaken by the Border Roads Organisation [BRO]. No new road construction or fresh alignment is being undertaken.

It is further clarified that the Yatra track runs along the right-hand side of the lake and is situated at a considerable distance from the lake. “It said the lake remains protected and the maintenance activity in question “was not intended to alter its character or ecological integrity”.

“The matter may, therefore, be viewed in its proper context, keeping in view the directions of the Hon’ble Supreme Court, the safety requirements of the annual pilgrimage and the longstanding nature of the track maintenance operations,” it added, while underlining that the maintenance and improvement of this track is a longstanding exercise undertaken regularly since 2012 and “not a new activity initiated in 2026”.

However, Opposition Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) president Mehbooba Mufti, who was denied permission to visit the spot with police citing security concerns, has asked the government to allow a team of politicians and experts to visit the Sheshnag lake.

“If the Union Territory [UT] government is relying on satellite images to claim that no construction is taking place at Sheshnag, why not allow us to visit the site and see for ourselves? The JCBs wreaking havoc there are visible for all to see. To dispel all doubts, let the Chief Minister depute a team of political leaders and environmentalists to inspect the site and establish the truth. What is there to hide?” said Ms. Mufti.

Meanwhile, referring to the allegations of irregularities in the Finance Accounts Assistant (FAA) examination conducted by the J&K Service Selection Board JKSSB), Mr. Abdullah said, “Political opponents were exploiting the concerns of unemployed youth and creating unnecessary mistrust about the recruitment process. I am always ready to admit if a mistake is committed. But when I dug deep into the matter, I found that instead of there being fraud in the examination, the fact is that the system worked properly. The paper did not leak. The paper was not stolen.”

Terming the incident as a case of “attempted cheating but disallowed”, Mr. Abdullah said, “There were people who tried to cheat in the examination. I agree with this. They took out the question paper from the examination hall, used wireless devices and tried to get answers. But they were caught on the spot. They were arrested. The JKSSB should have been praised for it,” said Mr. Abdullah.

articles.title: Senior advocate Syed Faisal Qadri appointed as J&K’s Advocate General after two year gap
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Mr. Faisal is a designated senior advocate with over 20 years of practice; the Omar Abdullah government in April had proposed the names for the post while the appointment came after the J&K High Court heard a PIL plea on November 5 regarding the vacant post

Senior advocate Syed Faisal Qadri was on Friday (November 27, 2026) appointed as the Advocate General of Jammu and Kashmir, eight months after the J&K government forwarded the proposal to Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha for his approval. The J&K government has been without an Advocate General for more than two years.

“In exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (1) of Section 79 of the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019 (Act No. 34 of 2019) and in supersession of notification S.O. No. 07 of 2019 dated 01-11-2019, the Lieutenant Governor of the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir is pleased to appoint Mr. Syed Faisal Qadri, Senior Advocate, as Advocate General for the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir,” reads the official order.

Mr. Qadri is a designated senior advocate with over 20 years of practice. With over 100 reported judgments, Mr. Faisal earned a name for himself by pleading cases of both private and government institutions in the J&K High Court and in the Supreme Court.

The Omar Abdullah government in April this year had proposed the names for the post. The appointment, however, came after the J&K High Court heard a public interest litigation (PIL) petition on November 5 regarding the vacant post. Senior Additional Advocate General Monika Kohli had apprised the Division Bench, comprising Chief Justice Pushpendra Singh Bhati and Justice Rajnesh Oswal, that the appointment would be made within a period of one month.

It is a major relief for Chief Minister Omar Abdullah whose government was pursuing many pending policy matters before the J&K High Court in the past two years. Mr. Abdullah’s party National Conference (NC) had won the Assembly elections in 2024, but remained without an Advocate General since then.
In 2019, senior advocate D.C. Raina was appointed as the Advocate General of J&K. He, later, tendered his resignation in October 2024.

articles.title: Centre proposes freeze on Lok Sabha seat proportions for States until 2051
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The new Constitutional Amendment Bill, accompanied by a fresh Delimitation Bill, proposes to increase the number of Lok Sabha seats in each State by 50%; they also bring into force the 33% reservation for women in the Lok Sabha

A new Constitutional Amendment Bill approved by the Union Cabinet on Friday (November 27, 2026) proposes an extension of the existing freeze on the inter-State distribution of Lok Sabha seats for another 25 years, until 2051, addressing the core concern of States that feared a loss of their proportionate strength due to the decline in their share of the national population.

The 132nd Constitutional Amendment Bill marks a significant turn from the 131st Amendment Bill moved by the Centre in April 2026 that sought to redistribute Lok Sabha seats among States according to the 2011 Census population.

The proposed amendment removes the linkage of the existing distribution of Lok Sabha seats to the 1971 Census and links it with provisions related to women’s reservation in Article 334A of the Constitution. The guarantee for a 50% increase in the number of Lok Sabha seats for each State is being written into this, providing that, for the purposes of giving immediate effect to such reservation for women, “the delimitation so undertaken shall provide for an increase of fifty per cent in the number of seats allocated to each State and Union territory in the House of the People.” The total number of seats in the Legislative Assembly of each State and Union territory will also increase similarly, “over and above the number of seats existing immediately before such delimitation”.

The new Bill, accompanied by a fresh Delimitation Bill, proposes to increase the number of Lok Sabha seats in each State by 50%, while the maximum strength of the lower House will rise from the current 550 to 850. If these Bills are passed by Parliament in its special sittings from November 30 to December 3, the path to immediate delimitation will open, which will also bring into force the 33% reservation for women in the Lok Sabha.
ALSO WATCH Cabinet clears delimitation Bill; is a two-thirds majority within reach? | Above the Fold | Nov 27, 2026

Amendments to Articles 81 and 82, which mandate the size and distribution of Lok Sabha seats among the States, propose to extend a sunset clause for the existing proportion until the first Census after 2051.

The existing provision in Article 82 that says that “until the relevant figures for the first census taken after the year 2026 have been published, it shall not be necessary to readjust” the distribution of seats is being amended in the Bill and will be changed to read “until the year 2051”.

Article 82 currently has two definitions for population: for the purposes of distribution among States, the 1971 population; and for the purposes of delimitation of individual constituencies within the States, the 2001 Census. The proposed amendment will extend the sunset clause to “until the year 2051”, but the reference to the 1971 Census has been dropped.

The Bill proposes that the distribution among States will be determined “in accordance with Article 334A”, while the boundaries of individual constituencies will be determined by the “latest published census figures available on the date of the commencement of the Constitution (One Hundred and Thirty-second Amendment) Act, 2026”.

articles.title: Broad-based pressure on food prices continues: RBI Bulletin
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: CPI inflation peaked to 6.1 % (y-o-y) in October 2026 from 5.5% in September 2026, slightly above the upper tolerance level of 6%–last observed in October 2024.
High-frequency data up to November 19 indicate continuing broad-based pressure on food prices, according to the November edition of the RBI Bulletin, released on Wednesday. .
Prices of all major cereals and pulses picked up. Edible oil prices recorded a broad-based increase, led by mustard oil, the RBI officials said in the State of the Economy article.

Vegetable prices presented a mixed picture, with onion prices rising moderately, tomato prices correcting sharply and potato prices picking up. The Indian basket of crude oil declined to $95 per barrel during November 1-18.
“The pressure on prices was primarily driven by ‘food and beverages’,” the officials pointed out.
Inflationary pressures were, however, not confined to food. Fuel and core inflation also firmed up, with 11 of the 12 CPI divisions registering sequential increases in October.

Within food and beverages, inflation rose across most sub-components, with notable spikes in vegetables, cereals, pulses and oils and fats, reflecting positive month-on-month price momentum. Fuel inflation recorded a relatively moderate uptick.

Geographically, inflation increased in both rural and urban areas in October, with food and beverages inflation remaining above 6% in both segments. While most States and Union Territories recorded inflation in the 4-6% range, the number reporting rates above 6% increased.

On the external front, geopolitical instability in West Asia continued to weigh on the global economic outlook. Although crude oil prices retreated from their October peaks, the absence of a durable peace kept markets volatile. “Apart from extant geopolitical risks, the recent pullback in AI stocks lends uncertainty to the global financial outlook,” the officials said.

Despite the challenging global environment and hawkish monetary policy stances adopted by major central banks, the RBI maintained that India’s domestic growth drivers and macroeconomic fundamentals remained important buffers.
“The Indian economy continues to maintain the resilience in economic activities as evident from high-frequency indicators,” they said.

articles.title: Net FDI fell to more than 5.5-year low in September 2026, as outflows jumped 40%
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: Despite September’s performance, net FDI in the first half of the financial year was more than 20% higher than in the same period last year

Net foreign direct investment (FDI) into India in September 2026 fell to its lowest level in at least 5.5 years, with outflows exceeding inflows by nearly $5 billion, data released by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) shows.

This was driven by a simultaneous slump in gross inflows and a jump in outflows. However, net FDI in the first half of the financial year (April-September 2026) was more than 20% higher than in the same period of the previous year.
September’s net FDI figure of -$4.95 billion was the lowest since at least March 2021, the earliest month for which data is accessible.

Direct investment refers to the inflows that give the investor substantial control over an asset or means of production, as opposed to portfolio investments, which are typically more in the nature of speculative purchases of minor shareholding.
Gross inflows, or the total amount of direct investment entering the country, fell to $5.9 billion in September 2026, 46.6% lower than in August, and 17.6% lower than in September of last year.

According to the RBI, around two-thirds of the gross inflows were channelled into manufacturing, communication, and computer services sectors, with Singapore and the U.S. as the major source countries.

Total outflows climbed to $10.8 billion in September 2026, nearly 40% higher than in August, and 15% higher than in September last year. Within this, repatriation of profits by foreign companies in India grew to $6.4 billion, nearly 37% higher than in the same month last year, and the highest since at least March 2021.
Outward investments made by Indian companies grew to a five-month high of $4.4 billion in September 2026.

The RBI says that of the outward investments, manufacturing, and financial, insurance and business services sectors accounted for about four-fifths of the amount that flowed out of India, with The Netherlands, Singapore and the U.S. serving as the major destinations.

📈 Economic, Banking & Finance 📅 28 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 3 Min Read

📰 Net FDI fell to more than 5.5-year low in September 2026, as outflows jumped 40%

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

Despite September’s performance, net FDI in the first half of the financial year was more than 20% higher than in the same period last year

Net foreign direct investment (FDI) into India in September 2026 fell to its lowest level in at least 5.5 years, with outflows exceeding inflows by nearly $5 billion, data released by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) shows.

This was driven by a simultaneous slump in gross inflows and a jump in outflows. However, net FDI in the first half of the financial year (April-September 2026) was more than 20% higher than in the same period of the previous year.

September’s net FDI figure of -$4.95 billion was the lowest since at least March 2021, the earliest month for which data is accessible.

Direct investment refers to the inflows that give the investor substantial control over an asset or means of production, as opposed to portfolio investments, which are typically more in the nature of speculative purchases of minor shareholding.

Gross inflows, or the total amount of direct investment entering the country, fell to $5.9 billion in September 2026, 46.6% lower than in August, and 17.6% lower than in September of last year.

According to the RBI, around two-thirds of the gross inflows were channelled into manufacturing, communication, and computer services sectors, with Singapore and the U.S. as the major source countries.

Total outflows climbed to $10.8 billion in September 2026, nearly 40% higher than in August, and 15% higher than in September last year. Within this, repatriation of profits by foreign companies in India grew to $6.4 billion, nearly 37% higher than in the same month last year, and the highest since at least March 2021.

Outward investments made by Indian companies grew to a five-month high of $4.4 billion in September 2026.

The RBI says that of the outward investments, manufacturing, and financial, insurance and business services sectors accounted for about four-fifths of the amount that flowed out of India, with The Netherlands, Singapore and the U.S. serving as the major destinations.

articles.title: Duty-free raw sugar imports up to 10 lakh tonnes allowed till March 2027
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: The industry expects more imports in the coming days and this will ensure supply of adequate quantity of sugar in the domestic market throughout the sugar season.

Duty-free imports of up to 10 lakh tonnes of raw sugar will be permitted until the end of March 2027, according to a notification issued by the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) on Wednesday.

A notification issued on August 20 had allowed duty-free imports of up to 10 lakh tonnes of sugar under the Tariff Rate Quota (TRQ) scheme until December 31, 2026. Separately, the DGFT has allowed sugar mills time until September 30, 2027, to process the imported raw sugar and sell it in the domestic market.

The Indian Sugar and Bio-Energy Manufacturers Association Director General Deepak Ballani told The Hindu that price parity had prevailed over the past, making it viable for Indian importers to source raw sugar from international markets, primarily Brazil. Some imports have already begun.

The industry expects more imports in the coming days and this will ensure supply of adequate quantity of sugar in the domestic market throughout the sugar season. It will also keep the prices stable, he said.

articles.title: Hamas says Israel tried to kill chief’s son in Gaza
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: ‘Izz al-Din al-Hayya, the youngest surviving son of Hamas political bureau chief Khalil al-Hayya, along with his family and the family of his late brother Azzam, survived an Israeli assassination attempt,’ a security source in Gaza told AFP

Hamas said Israel tried to kill an adult son of the Palestinian movement's chief, Khalil al-Hayya, in an overnight strike on Friday (November 27, 2026), with a Gaza security source telling AFP he survived.
Editorial | Damning report: On Justice Muralidhar’s report on Israeli atrocities
The strike follows a series of killings by the Israeli military in recent days that have targeted Hamas officials, despite a ceasefire in the war-shattered Palestinian territory.
Separately, Gaza's civil defence agency said Israeli forces killed seven people across the territory on Friday (November 27).

"Izz al-Din al-Hayya, the youngest surviving son of Hamas political bureau chief Khalil al-Hayya, along with his family and the family of his late brother Azzam, survived an Israeli assassination attempt early on Friday targeting a residential apartment in the Rimal neighbourhood, west of Gaza City," a security source in Gaza told AFP .
When asked by AFP , the Israeli military said it was looking into the incident.

Bassem Naim, a member of the Palestinian Islamist movement's political bureau, told AFP that "Israel's attempt to target the youngest son of Hamas political bureau chief Khalil al-Hayya... constitutes 'state terrorism,'" while Hamas issued a statement calling the targeting "cowardly".
Four of Mr. al-Hayya's sons have already been killed in Israeli attacks, including one in May and another in an Israeli strike targeting Hamas leaders in Doha in September 2025.

Gaza's civil defence agency, a rescue force which operates under Hamas authority, said an Israeli drone strike west of Rafah city in southern Gaza killed three people on Friday (November 27), with nearby Nasser Hospital confirming it received three bodies following the strike.
The Israeli military told AFP it had struck "three terrorists in the area".

articles.title: Global fashion brands shift orders from Bangladesh to India amid unrest
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Between November 1 and 18, brands diverted about $254 million worth ⁠of orders from Bangladesh, with most moving to neighbouring India, the owners said

Global fashion retailers including Zara and H&M shifted nearly a tenth of their monthly orders from ‌Bangladesh to other Asian manufacturing hubs in the first half of November, as labour unrest disrupted production and rising ​costs eroded the country’s competitive edge, three factory owners said.

Between November 1 and 18, brands diverted about $254 million worth ⁠of orders from Bangladesh, with most moving to neighbouring India, the owners said, a shift that represents a major blow to a key pillar of Bangladesh’s economy and could extend beyond the current unrest.

Industry leaders have said rising wages, energy shortages and political uncertainty have weakened the low-cost advantage that helped ‌make Bangladesh the world’s second apparel exporter after China, prompting global brands to diversify sourcing.

The protests have caused more than $400 million in production losses, according to the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA), in an industry that accounts for more ‌than 80% of Bangladesh’s export earnings and nearly 40% of its manufacturing jobs.
India has emerged ‌as ⁠the biggest beneficiary, while buyers are also looking to Vietnam, Cambodia and Indonesia to reduce supply-chain risks and improve delivery ⁠reliability, industry leaders said.
Those pressures intensified on Wednesday when Bangladesh approved a 36% increase in the minimum wage for garment workers, the smallest rise in four decades.

The increase fell well short of workers’ demands to more than double wages, triggering fresh clashes with police even as Abdur Rahman Tarafder, secretary of the Ministry of Labour and Employment, ​said the wage increase was “satisfactory” and that he hoped all ‌workers would resume work from Saturday.
Industry leaders said the increase would nevertheless narrow Bangladesh’s labour-cost advantage over India, although union groups argue the wages remain low by global industry standards.
Babul Akhter, a union leader and workers’ representative on the government-appointed wage board, said brands should not use the unrest to justify shifting orders out of Bangladesh.

He said retailers already factor political instability and labour ‌unrest into sourcing decisions, making such moves “hard to justify” and raising “serious doubts” whether the unrest was more than an excuse.

articles.title: Pressure tactics: On the new U.S. tariffs on India
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: The new U.S. tariffs must not erode India’s stand on a trade deal

The latest U.S. tariffs on India are nothing more than a pressure tactic to push for the signing of a trade deal. The U.S. Trade Representative (USTR) has proposed to levy a tariff of 25% for India’s apparent use of strategic excess manufacturing capacity to the detriment of American industry. This is the second-highest tariff rate the USTR has applied across the 14 countries that it has taken action against. The pressure on India does not come from the 25% rate but from the 17% this could be reduced to if it signs a trade deal with the U.S. This latest action is yet another example of how, despite the frothiness of India-U.S. trade relations over the past year and a half, the actual substance has not changed. The 25% rate now proposed, which is net of existing tariffs, is nearly the same as the 26% rate that U.S. President Donald Trump had first announced when he unveiled his ‘Liberation Day’ reciprocal tariffs in April 2025. Indeed, it is exactly the same as the 25% tariff he finally imposed in July 2025, before he imposed an additional 25% for India’s Russian oil imports. The 17% rate is also only marginally lower than the 18% that the two countries had agreed on in their joint statement in February 2026. It is also just one percentage point lower than the tariffs on competitors such as Indonesia and Malaysia. The allegation of India having excess capacity does not hold water. Indeed, were India to have excess manufacturing capacity in any sector, it would be the Government of India that would be the first to announce it with great fanfare, instead of denying it as it did. After all, that has been its aim since 2014.

Yet, even a basic assessment of India’s import dependence and the fact that manufacturing’s share in GDP is lower now than a decade ago shows that India is far from having excess manufacturing capacity in any sector. Further, higher tariffs are unlikely to reduce America’s imports of the goods from India that it does depend on. The USTR mentioned generic pharmaceuticals, telecommunication equipment, and renewable energy goods. The first two are items that India has developed expertise in, which is distinct from strategic excess capacity. A relatively small tariff disadvantage will not substantially erode the attractiveness of these Indian products. Renewable energy imports from India have swelled because the U.S. is reducing its purchases from China. Hanging over all of this are the 100% tariffs related to the purchase of Russian oil, which have only temporarily been paused. India has so far held off on signing a deal, and must go ahead with one only if it is convinced that the benefits at least equal the costs.

✍️ Editorial & Opinion 📅 27 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 4 Min Read

📰 Pressure tactics: On the new U.S. tariffs on India

🎯 Exam Relevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions

The new U.S. tariffs must not erode India’s stand on a trade deal

The latest U.S. tariffs on India are nothing more than a pressure tactic to push for the signing of a trade deal. The U.S. Trade Representative (USTR) has proposed to levy a tariff of 25% for India’s apparent use of strategic excess manufacturing capacity to the detriment of American industry. This is the second-highest tariff rate the USTR has applied across the 14 countries that it has taken action against. The pressure on India does not come from the 25% rate but from the 17% this could be reduced to if it signs a trade deal with the U.S. This latest action is yet another example of how, despite the frothiness of India-U.S. trade relations over the past year and a half, the actual substance has not changed. The 25% rate now proposed, which is net of existing tariffs, is nearly the same as the 26% rate that U.S. President Donald Trump had first announced when he unveiled his ‘Liberation Day’ reciprocal tariffs in April 2025. Indeed, it is exactly the same as the 25% tariff he finally imposed in July 2025, before he imposed an additional 25% for India’s Russian oil imports. The 17% rate is also only marginally lower than the 18% that the two countries had agreed on in their joint statement in February 2026. It is also just one percentage point lower than the tariffs on competitors such as Indonesia and Malaysia. The allegation of India having excess capacity does not hold water. Indeed, were India to have excess manufacturing capacity in any sector, it would be the Government of India that would be the first to announce it with great fanfare, instead of denying it as it did. After all, that has been its aim since 2014.

Yet, even a basic assessment of India’s import dependence and the fact that manufacturing’s share in GDP is lower now than a decade ago shows that India is far from having excess manufacturing capacity in any sector. Further, higher tariffs are unlikely to reduce America’s imports of the goods from India that it does depend on. The USTR mentioned generic pharmaceuticals, telecommunication equipment, and renewable energy goods. The first two are items that India has developed expertise in, which is distinct from strategic excess capacity. A relatively small tariff disadvantage will not substantially erode the attractiveness of these Indian products. Renewable energy imports from India have swelled because the U.S. is reducing its purchases from China. Hanging over all of this are the 100% tariffs related to the purchase of Russian oil, which have only temporarily been paused. India has so far held off on signing a deal, and must go ahead with one only if it is convinced that the benefits at least equal the costs.

articles.title: Indefensible defiance: On Tamil Nadu and Court’s Thirupparankundram order
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: Tamil Nadu should have followed Court order without backing Deepathoon claim

By defying the Supreme Court’s one-time direction to also light the ceremonial Karthigai Deepam at a stone pillar , claimed by Hindu groups to be a Deepathoon, atop the Thirupparankundram hills, the Tamil Nadu government has disregarded a constitutional body’s authority. Believed to be Lord Murugan’s first abode, the hills have, for centuries , witnessed an intersection of religious faiths, with occasional skirmishes leading to tense flare-ups and legal battles. They house the Arulmigu Subramaniya Swamy, Uchchi Pillaiyar and Kashi Viswanathar temples; Sultan Sikkandar Avulia Dargah; and also Jain beds. Historically, the lamp is lit near the Pillaiyar temple. In 1994-95, the Hindu Munnani precipitated matters, claiming that the moksha deepam (for departed souls) and Karthigai Deepam were being lit at the same place. It demanded the lamp be lit at a pillar, 50 metres from the Dargah. In multiple legal battles, successive governments, backed by hereditary priests (Sthaneeka Bhattars) , opposed the demand. Even in 1862 and 1912, courts had disallowed lamp lighting near the Dargah. The BJP and its affiliates have, since, aggressively weaponised the demand in the name of Hindu religious rights.

Against this backdrop, last year, the Madras High Cour t’s Madurai Bench, relying on the 1931 Privy Council ruling on ownership of the hills, held that “for the sake of protecting its property, the [Subramania Swamy] temple management is obliged to light the festival lamp at the Deepathoon” . The DMK government defied the order. Later, a Division Bench upheld the verdict. While staying this order recently, the Supreme Court cited the festival’s proximity to permit the lamp to be lit at the Deepathoon this year alone , clarifying that this did not constitute “essential religious practice”. The State filed a review petition , arguing when no right is recognised prima facie, a direction altering the existing position lacks judicial foundation. On Karthigai Deepam day, November 24, with the review pending, the government walked a tightrope. The Collector assured the High Court of compliance. Yet, the lamp was lit only at the traditional spot . The Collector has now apologised to the Court, blaming the temple’s Board of Trustees for not authorising the proposed lighting team at the Deepathoon. The administration has thus attempted to distinguish its proclaimed intent to comply with judicial directions from customs governed by the trustees. But it remains exposed to the charge of colluding with the temple authorities to breach a judicial mandate. The Deepathoon may be a mischievous prop deployed by self-serving Hindu groups, but the pillar stands on temple property. The State could have permitted the limited lighting, leaving the onus on the Court, without endorsing the Deepathoon claim or compromising religious amity. A democracy can remain healthy only when its constitutional pillars do not collide with one another.

They house the Arulmigu Subramaniya Swamy, Uchchi Pillaiyar and Kashi Viswanathar temples; Sultan Sikkandar Avulia Dargah; and also Jain beds. Historically, the lamp is lit near the Pillaiyar temple. In 1994-95, the Hindu Munnani precipitated matters, claiming that the moksha deepam (for departed souls) and Karthigai Deepam were being lit at the same place. It demanded the lamp be lit at a pillar, 50 metres from the Dargah. In multiple legal battles, successive governments, backed by hereditary priests (Sthaneeka Bhattars) , opposed the demand. Even in 1862 and 1912, courts had disallowed lamp lighting near the Dargah. The BJP and its affiliates have, since, aggressively weaponised the demand in the name of Hindu religious rights.
• Against this backdrop, last year, the Madras High Cour t’s Madurai Bench, relying on the 1931 Privy Council ruling on ownership of the hills, held that “for the sake of protecting its property, the [Subramania Swamy] temple management is obliged to light the festival lamp at the Deepathoon” . The DMK government defied the order. Later, a Division Bench upheld the verdict. While staying this order recently, the Supreme Court cited the festival’s proximity to permit the lamp to be lit at the Deepathoon this year alone , clarifying that this did not constitute “essential religious practice”. The State filed a review petition , arguing when no right is recognised prima facie, a direction altering the existing position lacks judicial foundation. On Karthigai Deepam day, November 24, with the review pending, the government walked a tightrope. The Collector assured the High Court of compliance. Yet, the lamp was lit only at the traditional spot . The Collector has now apologised to the Court, blaming the temple’s Board of Trustees for not authorising the proposed lighting team at the Deepathoon. The administration has thus attempted to distinguish its proclaimed intent to comply with judicial directions from customs governed by the trustees. But it remains exposed to the charge of colluding with the temple authorities to breach a judicial mandate. The Deepathoon may be a mischievous prop deployed by self-serving Hindu groups, but the pillar stands on temple property. The State could have permitted the limited lighting, leaving the onus on the Court, without endorsing the Deepathoon claim or compromising religious amity. A democracy can remain healthy only when its constitutional pillars do not collide with one another.

articles.title: Amended Delimitation Bill likely to be tabled in special Parliament sitting from November 30
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Centre announces special sitting of Parliament from November 30, 2026, over 100 days since both Houses were adjourned without prorogation; government trying to pass the Bill after ‘operation lotus’, says Congress
The government has called for a special sitting of Parliament beginning Monday (November 30, 2026), where it is likely to table an amended Delimitation Bill.

The two Houses will meet on separate dates, Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju announced on Thursday (November 26, 2026), which is the 104th day since the Monsoon Session adjourned indefinitely on August 13.

Lok Sabha sittings will begin on November 30 and Rajya Sabha sittings on December 2. Both Houses will conclude on December 3. The last record of a session of Parliament continuing unprorogued was in 2008 , when it went on for 87 days.

The Union Cabinet will meet on Friday (November 27, 2026) to clear the amended legislation. According to sources, three crucial changes are being introduced: a uniform 50% increase in the share of Lok Sabha seats; extending the freeze for 25 years on using the 1971 Census as the basis to determine the proportional strength of each State in the Lok Sabha; and third, using the 2011 Census for redrawing constituencies within each State. This replicates the formula brought by the Atal Bihari Vajpayee government in the Constitution (Eighty-fourth Amendment) Act, 2001.

Reacting to the announcement, Congress general secretary (communication) Jairam Ramesh said the Narendra Modi government announced the session “after 105 days of operation lotus” in the hope of getting a “super-tainted” two-thirds majority to get the Bill passed. “Can there be a great insult to and assault on the Constitution,” he asked in a post on X, noting that the announcement came on Constitution Day.
Congress general secretary (organisation) K.C. Venugopal took to X to describe the attempt to pass the Delimitation Bill as “ sansad chori” .
“To orchestrate this murder of the Constitution on Constitution Day shows how badly they want to mock our precious democratic system. We will not allow this to pass,” Mr. Venugopal said.

Since April, when the legislative package, including the Delimitation Bill, was defeated by a united Opposition in the Lok Sabha, the seat arithmetic in the House has changed. Twenty TMC MPs broke away and merged with the Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI), pledging support to the NDA. TMC challenged the split, which is currently under Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla’s review. The NCPI faction, on Tuesday (November 24, 2026), 84 days after TMC’s challenge, submitted replies to Mr. Birla, defending its decision and asserting that the move did not violate any parliamentary or constitutional provisions.

Six Shiv Sena (UBT) MPs joined the Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena. Following the recent alliance between the BJP and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD), the lone SAD MP is also expected to vote with the government. It is also learnt that the YSR Congress, which has four MPs in the Lok Sabha, will extend support to the government on the Bill.
In this evolving situation, all eyes are on the DMK, with 22 Lok Sabha MPs, and the NCP (Sharadchandra Pawar), with eight.

articles.title: Sthaneeka Bhattars make contradictory statements on the lighting of deepam
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: On November 24, the Executive Officer of the Subramaniya Swamy Temple at Thirupparankundram had said the reasoning for lighting the lamp at the Deepa Mandapam was backed by the Bhattars. But a letter purportedly written by the Bhattars, stating that they had not given any letter of consent, went viral on social media the next day

The Sthaneeka Bhattars of the Subramaniya Swamy Temple at Thirupparankundram gave some tense moments to the Madurai district administration by making contradictory statements on their “consent” for lighting the ceremonial lamp at the traditional spot — Deepa Mandapam — on Karthigai Deepam day.
Editorial | Indefensible defiance: On Tamil Nadu and Court’s Thirupparankundram order

The administration had submitted at the Supreme Court that despite its readiness to light the lamp at the deepathoon , it could not comply with the court directive as the temple’s Board of Trustees insisted on lighting the lamp only at the Deepa Mandapam, following age-old practices, customs and rituals, and agama rules.

A statement made on November 24 by the temple’s Executive Officer, G. Selvi, had said the reasoning for lighting the lamp at the Deepa Mandapam was backed by the Bhattars. However, the next day, a letter purportedly written by the Bhattars, stating that they had not given any letter of consent on lighting the lamp on November 24, went viral on social media. They said they had given consent for lighting the lamp at the usual spot near Uchipillaiyar Temple “last year” (2025). The recent statement by the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department referring to their consent, made “without consulting” them, had caused mental agony, they said.

Meanwhile, there was commotion outside the house of Swaminatha Bhattar late in the evening on Wednesday, as functionaries of the BJP and Hindu outfits arrived at the priest’s house. Temple officials too were present at the house. The BJP functionaries said the Bhattars were being “forced” to give a new letter of consent to help the officials substantiate their stand before the Supreme Court. The demonstrators were detained by the police.

An official of the Department said the Bhattars gave the new letter on Wednesday to the Board of Trustees. “The lighting of Karthigai Deepam has been done at the Uchipillaiyar Temple since 1996 with the cooperation of the temple authorities,” said the letter, signed by four Bhattars. However, they underlined that they were only replying to a letter written by the temple administration, seeking their opinion on this issue.

On November 24, the Executive Officer of the Subramaniya Swamy Temple at Thirupparankundram had said the reasoning for lighting the lamp at the Deepa Mandapam was backed by the Bhattars. But a letter purportedly written by the Bhattars, stating that they had not given any letter of consent, went viral on social media the next day

The Sthaneeka Bhattars of the Subramaniya Swamy Temple at Thirupparankundram gave some tense moments to the Madurai district administration by making contradictory statements on their “consent” for lighting the ceremonial lamp at the traditional spot — Deepa Mandapam — on Karthigai Deepam day.

Editorial | Indefensible defiance: On Tamil Nadu and Court’s Thirupparankundram order

The administration had submitted at the Supreme Court that despite its readiness to light the lamp at the deepathoon , it could not comply with the court directive as the temple’s Board of Trustees insisted on lighting the lamp only at the Deepa Mandapam, following age-old practices, customs and rituals, and agama rules.

A statement made on November 24 by the temple’s Executive Officer, G. Selvi, had said the reasoning for lighting the lamp at the Deepa Mandapam was backed by the Bhattars. However, the next day, a letter purportedly written by the Bhattars, stating that they had not given any letter of consent on lighting the lamp on November 24, went viral on social media. They said they had given consent for lighting the lamp at the usual spot near Uchipillaiyar Temple “last year” (2025). The recent statement by the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department referring to their consent, made “without consulting” them, had caused mental agony, they said.

Meanwhile, there was commotion outside the house of Swaminatha Bhattar late in the evening on Wednesday, as functionaries of the BJP and Hindu outfits arrived at the priest’s house. Temple officials too were present at the house. The BJP functionaries said the Bhattars were being “forced” to give a new letter of consent to help the officials substantiate their stand before the Supreme Court. The demonstrators were detained by the police.

An official of the Department said the Bhattars gave the new letter on Wednesday to the Board of Trustees. “The lighting of Karthigai Deepam has been done at the Uchipillaiyar Temple since 1996 with the cooperation of the temple authorities,” said the letter, signed by four Bhattars. articles.title: Madras High Court commends Tamil Nadu police for tracing 2,510 missing persons within a fortnight
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Justices A.D. Jagadish Chandira and B. Karthikeyan record their appreciation for a special drive conducted by the police to trace missing men, women, boys and girls

The Madras High Court on Thursday (November 26, 2026) commended the Tamil Nadu police for conducting a two-week-long special drive to trace missing persons and succeeding in tracing 1,469 women, 629 men, 289 girls and 128 boys between October 30, 2026 and November 13, 2026.

Justices A.D. Jagadish Chandira and B. Karthikeyan recorded appreciation to the police department for having traced as many as 2,510 missing persons during the special drive and asked Additional Public Prosecutor M. Mohamed Riyaz to ensure that the momentum sustains.

It was while hearing a habeas corpus petition filed by T. Bhuvaneshwari of Keezhaiyur in Kallakurichi district, whose husband P. Sankararaj was missing since 2021, that the judges had called for data related to missing persons from the office of the Director General of Police/Head of Police Force.

In response, A. Pradeep, Assistant Inspector General of Police (Law and Order) and staff officer to the DGP/HoPF, filed a report before the court on Thursday stating that 2,41,927 cases were booked in Tamil Nadu in connection with the missing of 2,63,894 missing persons between January 1, 2016 and November 16, 2026.

Of them, 2,48,364 missing persons had been traced and reunited with their family members and the rest of 15,530 remain untraceable. The court was also told that as on November 16, 2026 15,134 cases related to missing persons were under investigation and of them, 1,064 cases were more than seven years old.

The court was also told that 1,174 cases were between seven and five years old; 2,121 cases were between five and three years old; 4,402 cases were between three and one year old; and 2,861 cases were three months old. The district-wise data regarding the status of missing person cases was also submitted before the court.

On the court’s query as to whether latest technologies such as Artificial Intelligence were being utilised for tracing the missing persons, the office of the DGP/HoPF said, the Tamil Nadu citizen portal www.police.tn.gov.in provides a facility for searching and comparing missing-person particulars with the available database of unidentified dead bodies.

If the users enter basic details of missing individuals such as gender, age group, date range of disappearance, identifiable marks and physical parameters, the system returns a list of unidentified deceased persons that match the entered criteria. Photographs and physical descriptions are also displayed to enable manual comparison by families or police officials, the AIG said.
He told the court that a facial recognition system was utlised for comparison of available photographs with the existing database to identify possible matches.

Further, the DGP/HoPF’s office had circualted a Standard Operating Procedure on August 10, 2026 for utilisation of CCTV footage, call detail records, internet protocol detail records, social-media information, banking transactions, cybercrime-related information, missing-person portals, NATGRID and other relevant digital evidence, wherever necessary and permissible under law, for tracing missing children, Mr. Pradeep added.

articles.title: Tamil Nadu govt. has acquired only 24% of land required for railway projects: Ashwini Vaishnav
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Stating that the Tamil Nadu government will have to do its duty of acquiring land if all sanctioned railway projects are to be implemented in the State, Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said that the total land acquired so far stood at only 24% of the land required.

Speaking at a Constitution Day event organised by the State BJP unit in the city on Thursday, Mr. Vaishnav said, that out of a total requirment of 4,800 hectares of land, the State has managed to acquire only 1,253 hectares. “My request to the TVK is, please take this as a challenge. Acquire the land [and] we will [carry out] each and every project without any hassle...don’t shy away from your responsibilities,” he emphasised. Projects sanctioned for development of railways in Tamil Nadu amounted to Rs. 48,000 crore, he added.

Taking a dig at the State government over the Thiruparankundram deepam issue, Mr. Vaishnav said, “You can stop one deepam to be lighted, but you cannot stop the Tamil people from progress. Stopping one deepam, you have disturbed the emotions of millions of people.”

Listing out some of the projects undertaken, the minister said that 77 railway stations in Tamil Nadu are being reconstructed. articles.title: Experts examine key aspects, challenges of conducting Census
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: An engaging conversation between retired IAS officer C. Chandramouli and Vinay Sitapati, Associate Dean and Professor of Law and Politics at Shiv Nadar University, over the former’s book, Counting a Nation – The Story of the Indian Census, here on Thursday evening, brought out the various aspects of conducting Census in the country.

Among the issues discussed were the need for a law to govern enumeration for caste census, the challenges faced while ensuring accuracy, training of enumerators for a standardised enumeration process, differences in the motive for carrying out the Census before and after the country’s independence, and the implication of Census for delimitation.

During the book launch organised by Chennai International Centre (CIC) at the NFDC Tagore auditorium, Mr. Chandramouli, who had also served as the Registrar General and the Census Commissioner of India, recalled the challenges faced by enumerators while collecting data, specifically while enumerating the Sentinelese.
Mr. Chandramouli, also the CIC Managing Director, explained why his book was not a memoir, noting that carrying out the Census was a team work of greater proportion.
Mr. Sitapati said Mr. Chandramouli’s book was a current affairs work, but it looked at current issues through the lens of history.
The discussion also highlighted the curiosity over the results of Census 2027.

When a curious Mr. Sitapati asked what the newspapers’ headlines would be, especially that of The Hindu, the day after Census 2027 results, Mr. Chandramouli said the headlines would differ across regions depending on the results for each State.

As for adopting technology for conducting Census, Mr. Chandramouli said that even in the most sophisticated of Censuses, “ground truthing of the whole exercise by visiting the field and checking the information is key to the success of an operation like this.”
With modern technology, the exercise could be more efficient and quicker, he added.

articles.title: Mercury in cosmetics: What does the Keralam case reveal about health risks of skin-lightening creams | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: What does the recent case in Keralam reveal about mercury poisoning from cosmetics? How does exposure affect the kidneys, and what safeguards are in place to regulate unsafe products?

The quest for beauty and the enduring appeal for fair and blemishfree skin goes back to ages and across cultures. However, in recent years, this has been landing people in hospitals with serious health issues, as it happened in the case of the 17-year-old girl from Areekode in Malappuram district in Keralam.

Persuaded by many social influencers who raved about a face cream which gave them fair, blemishfree skin, she had also been using the same for over a year. The product with the brand name F-TUNES - claimed to contain turmeric and other “natural ingredients” and cited Dubai as the place of manufacture. She was hospitalised after she developed severe symptoms like fainting spells, swelling on legs and fall in blood pressure and was diagnosed with Membranous nephropathy, a condition wherein the immune system gets dysregulated, triggering nephrotic syndrome (heavy loss of protein through urine). Doctors traced her condition to the heavy mercury content in the face cream she was using. Lab analysis of a sample of the skin lightning cream obtained from the patient revealed that the product contained 12,500 ppm of mercury, way over the legal limit of 1 ppm

After prolonged treatment, the girl is now recovering. The police and drug regulatory authorities have begun a crackdown on the dubious cosmetic products in the market . The Health Minister has also threatened action against social influencers who are peddling dubious cosmetics online

What does the recent case in Keralam reveal about mercury poisoning from cosmetics? How does exposure affect the kidneys, and what safeguards are in place to regulate unsafe products?

The quest for beauty and the enduring appeal for fair and blemishfree skin goes back to ages and across cultures. However, in recent years, this has been landing people in hospitals with serious health issues, as it happened in the case of the 17-year-old girl from Areekode in Malappuram district in Keralam.

Persuaded by many social influencers who raved about a face cream which gave them fair, blemishfree skin, she had also been using the same for over a year. The product with the brand name F-TUNES - claimed to contain turmeric and other “natural ingredients” and cited Dubai as the place of manufacture. She was hospitalised after she developed severe symptoms like fainting spells, swelling on legs and fall in blood pressure and was diagnosed with Membranous nephropathy, a condition wherein the immune system gets dysregulated, triggering nephrotic syndrome (heavy loss of protein through urine). Doctors traced her condition to the heavy mercury content in the face cream she was using. Lab analysis of a sample of the skin lightning cream obtained from the patient revealed that the product contained 12,500 ppm of mercury, way over the legal limit of 1 ppm

After prolonged treatment, the girl is now recovering. The police and drug regulatory authorities have begun a crackdown on the dubious cosmetic products in the market . The Health Minister has also threatened action against social influencers who are peddling dubious cosmetics online

articles.title: Kallakurichi MLA-woman IAS officer harassment case in Tamil Nadu: a timeline
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Here’s a timeline of how the Kallakurichi MLA-IAS officer row in Tamil Nadu unfolded, the Opposition’s charges and more

Tamil Nadu’s Kallakurichi MLA C. Arul Vignesh has been at the centre of a political storm after he was accused of and booked on charges of misbehaving with a woman IAS officer. However, Mr. Vignesh, an MLA of the ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) in Tamil Nadu , denied the charges earlier this month (November 2026).

It is alleged that the TVK MLA Arul Vignesh sent an inappropriate message to the woman IAS officer and behaved in an indecent manner under the influence of alcohol at her official residence. The issue first surfaced on social media.

Here’s a timeline of how the Kallakurichi MLA-woman IAS officer row unfolded, the allegations against the TVK legislator, the Opposition’s charges and more about the case that has stirred controversy in a major embarrassment for Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay-led TVK government that has come to power for the first time.

November 9, 2026 — DMK Parliamentary Party leader Kanimozhi Karunanidhi puts up a post on X, pointing out claims on social media that the TVK MLA had sent an inappropriate message to the officer and had visited her residence in an inebriated state. She demands a response from the TVK president and Chief Minister Mr. Vijay on the issue.

November 10, 2026 — Kallakurichi MLA Arul Vignesh denies the charges and insists that the allegations made against him on social media were part of the “dirty politics” played by the Opposition. “I have always maintained high respect for government officers. False messages are being spread against me on social media,” he said.

November 12, 2026 — The DMK submits a petition to the Director-General of Police (DGP), demanding action against Mr. Arul Vignesh over the allegations. DMK president M.K. Stalin says Mr. Vijay should take ‘real action’ against the erring MLA.

November 12, 2026 — Tamil Nadu Minister for Law and Energy Resources C.T.R. Nirmal Kumar denies the allegations against the TVK MLA. Responding to allegations made by Kanimozhi, he said it was condemnable and inappropriate on her part to make a statement based on the rumour she had come across on social media.

November 13, 2026 — Tamil Nadu Social Justice Minister Vanni Arasu, who is the Minister in-charge for Kallakurichi district , says there is a responsibility to protect women entering public life and those working in government service. Arasu, who belongs to VCK, an ally of the TVK, says, “The VCK has always stood with victims and on the side of justice.”

November 15, 2026 — The National Commission for Women takes suo moto cognisance of the allegations and asks the DGP to conduct an impartial inquiry. The Commission calls for a detailed Action Taken Report (ATR) within seven days.

November 23, 2026 — State Public Prosecutor (SPP) R. John Sathyan submits before the Madras High Court that neither Chief Secretary M. Sai Kumar nor the police had received any representation/complaint from the woman IAS officer while it was earlier alleged that the woman IAS officer submitted a complaint to the Chief Secretary on July 31. The submission was made during the hearing of a writ petition (criminal) filed by advocate R. Thrishuli, who had sought a direction to the police to register a case.

articles.title: No need for CBI probe in Kallakurichi TVK MLA case: Thirumavalavan
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Tamil Nadu government is taking appropriate legal action, says VCK leader

Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi (VCK) founder Thol. Thirumavalavan on Thursday (November 26, 2026) said there was no need for a CBI probe into the allegations that the Kallakurichi TVK MLA had sent inappropriate messages to a District Collector. He said the Tamil Nadu government was taking appropriate legal action.

Speaking to journalists at Chennai, he said the VCK had consistently maintained that strict action should be taken against the MLA if he had sent messages to the Collector in a manner that caused mental distress.

“We have now received confirmation that a District Collector has formally lodged a complaint. Following this, the government has acted swiftly, registered a case against the particular MLA and initiated an investigation . We do not see any need for the CBI to intervene at this stage,” he said.

Responding to questions about the alleged delay in taking action, with 116 days having elapsed since the incident, Mr. Thirumavalavan said it was important to distinguish between the date of the alleged incident and the date on which the formal complaint was lodged.

“The incident came to light through the media and social media. The information available to us is that the Collector lodged a formal complaint only recently . We also learnt through social media reports that, when the incident occurred, she had not submitted a written complaint but had sought that the MLA be called and warned,” he contended.

He was responding to allegations that the Collector had earlier brought the matter to the attention of the Chief Secretary, who had allegedly attempted to persuade her to seek a transfer to another district. Opposition parties have cited the alleged delay and the handling of the complaint as reasons for seeking a CBI probe.

“Now that she has come forward and lodged a complaint, I believe the government is acting swiftly. A case has been registered under the appropriate sections, and I am confident that legal action will follow,” Mr. Thirumavalavan said.

articles.title: Several people of Kotia villages asked to appear before Koraput Sub Collector’s office
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The police cases and hefty surety amount shocked people living in Ganjaibhadra, Pagaluchennuru and Pattuchennuru villages

Hundreds of villagers living in Kotia group of villages are eagerly waiting for the Andhra Pradesh government’s response with regard to arrests and bind over cases filed against the people who wanted to be under the administrative jurisdiction of AP.

Ahead of AP’s scheduled panchayat elections on December 2 , 2026, the Odisha government has put notices on walls of the houses of villagers, asking them to attend for the hearing of cases at Koraput sub collector’s office on November 27, 2026 (Friday).

According to locals, the villagers including Bachhala Prasada Rao, Tadangi Rajesh, Gemmala Bheeshu, Tadangi Sannam, Chodipilli Raju, Gemmala Somulu, B. Adilakshmi, G. Lakshmi, Chinta Ramulu and others received notices and were asked to deposit Rs.1.5 lakh surety amount to get bails.
The police cases and hefty surety amount shocked people living in Ganjaibhadra, Pagaluchennuru and Pattuchennuru villages where the panchayat elections would be held on December 2, 2026.
Recently, the locals had a heated argument with Odisha police and revenue officials during the ZPTC/MPTC elections while clearly mentioning that they would like to be with AP government.

It is said that this was the main reason for the Odisha police to give notices ahead of Panchayat elections. The villagers who are happy with AP government’s welfare schemes are keen to take part in panchayat elections. They alleged that the Odisha government was trying to disrupt the election process and make people remain indoors on the day of elections.

Former Deputy Chief Minister Peedika Rajanna Dora alleged that AP government’s inaction and silence over the harassment had given an opportunity for the Odisha to file false cases against the innocent villagers.
While speaking to The Hindu over telephone, he said that NDA government’s are in power both in AP and Odisha and were supposed to resolve the issue instead of causing mental agony to local people.

“The Center should resolve the jurisdiction issue to put an end to the controversy that has been in existence almost since Independence. Otherwise, the people will continue to face many troubles,” said Mr. Rajanna Dora who is former MLA of Salur.

The present Salur MLA and Minister for Tribal Welfare Gummadi Sandhya Rani expressed displeasure over the filing of cases against the villagers. Meanwhile, Parvatipuram-Manyam district hoped that the elections would be conducted in spite of the strong objection from the Odisha government while referring to good response for MPTC/ZPTC elections in Kotia group of villages on November 5, 2026.

articles.title: Bangladesh’s Opposition party blasts Australian media reports over leader’s visit
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The party said the legal notice sent to The Australian newspaper pointed out ‘seven defamatory imputations and demands corrections, retraction of the report, an apology and the preservation of relevant documents’

Bangladesh’s main Opposition party, Jamaat-e-Islami, has sent a legal notice to a major Australian newspaper for publishing a report against its party chief, who has returned from the country, cutting short his overseas tour amid a controversy over his visit.

In a statement, the party late on Thursday (November 28, 2026) said the legal notice sent to The Australian newspaper pointed out “seven defamatory imputations and demands corrections, retraction of the report, an apology and the preservation of relevant documents” involving Jamaat Ameer Shafiqur Rahman’s tour.

“The publisher has been asked to provide a written response within 48 hours,” the statement said but did not explain what measure the party would take if the news outlet did not comply with the demand.

The report by The Australian described Mr. Rahman as a "Hamas-praising Bangladesh Islamist leader" and criticised the Australian government for allowing him into the country without stricter visa screening.
The Jamaat firmly rejected the report and said Mr. Rahman's early return was due to pressing organisational commitments in Bangladesh.
The Jamaat chief reached Sydney on November 20 as part of a weeklong overseas tour to Australia and Malaysia.
In Australia, he was scheduled to hold meetings with senior Australian government officials in Canberra and join receptions and community gatherings.

But a major media and diplomatic controversy erupted on November 23 when The Australian published a report titled “Sinwar was a hero': Fury as Hamas-praising Bangladesh Islamist leader arrives. Other Australian Jewish and Hindu advocacy groups alleged that he has in the past made statements comparing working women to prostitutes and eulogising former Hamas leader Yahya Sinwar.

Jamaat secretary general Mia Golam Porwar called the report "false, misleading and defamatory". His foreign affairs advisor and lawmaker Barrister Mir Ahmad Bin Quasem sent the formal legal notice to the publisher of The Australian .

Mr. Porwar said the entire report was based on the application seeking the cancellation of Mr. Rahman’s visa by an immigration representative and “it is understood that the individual in question is the writer and director of Baba, a film glorifying (Bangladesh’s founder) Sheikh Mujibur Rahman and his family”.

articles.title: Major storm batters U.S. on Thanksgiving holiday; 400 flights cancelled
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: New York’s famed Macy’s parade was postponed for the first time in its 100-year history

A powerful storm disrupted Thanksgiving celebrations for millions of Americans on Thursday (November 26, 2026), as New York’s famed Macy’s parade was postponed for the first time in its 100-year history.
Heavy rain and strong winds from the “Nor-easter” battered the central and eastern United States, creating treacherous travel conditions during one of the country’s busiest holiday periods.

As families were gathering for traditional holiday feasts, more than 900,000 homes and businesses were without power, with Pennsylvania, Maryland and Virginia particularly hard hit, according to tracking website PowerOutage.
At airports, nearly 400 flights were canceled and over 2,000 were delayed in the United States, mostly in the East, figures from FlightAware showed.

New York’s famed parade, which sees brightly colored balloons travel through the heart of Manhattan, was pushed back to Saturday (November 28, 2026) due to what organizers said was an “abundance of caution.”

Millions of people typically gather to catch a glimpse of the festivities. The only other time the parade was not held on Thanksgiving Thursday was when it was canceled for three years during World War II.

Organizers would have been only too aware of the gusting winds that wrecked the parade back in 1997 when a careening 18-foot figure of the “Cat in the Hat” toppled a lamppost, knocking one bystander unconscious.

“While we are heartbroken that our parade was postponed, the safety of our partners, the safety of our participants — and spectators — is and always will be our top priority,” said Macy’s parade executive producer Will Coss.
While flooding was reported up and down the East Coast, impacts were also felt inland, with powerful gusts and inundated soil leading to trees tumbling over onto power lines and homes.
Authorities in the Maryland suburbs of the US capital, worried about the impact of power outages on the water treatment network, asked nearly two million customers to conserve tap water consumption.

articles.title: President Donald Trump insists Nvidia CEO not a security threat
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Jensen Huang sudden resignation saw the stock price of Nvidia plummet, before a shock decision by the board to reinstate him saw a partial rebound

U.S. President Donald Trump said on Thursday (November 26, 2026) that he had seen sufficient information that Nvidia’s Jensen Huang was not a security threat, while touting his administration’s intervention to save the scandal-plagued CEO’s job as “a great thing” for the world.
“I think he’s absolutely fine,” Mr. Trump told reporters at his Mar-a-Lago estate.

Asked by AFP how he could be sure when the Justice Department would not confirm it had conducted a thorough investigation into Mr. Huang, Mr. Trump said his belief was based on “information I have, which is a lot of information.”
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's return brings open-weight AI debate to forefront in Washington
Jensen Huang won’t need a pardon, says U.S. Vice President, as scrutiny of Nvidia scandal builds in Washington
How Jensen Huang’s affair puts Nvidia and American AI at risk? (Recorded before his resignation) | In Focus Podcast

Mr. Huang, a key figure in the AI revolution, was forced to resign earlier this month after revelations that he had an affair with a business executive who reportedly has ties to Chinese intelligence and whose company may have helped China obtain advanced chips in violation of U.S. export controls.
His sudden resignation saw the stock price of Nvidia plummet , before a shock decision by the board to reinstate him saw a partial rebound .

Mr. Trump revealed that he and other officials in his administration have worked behind the scenes to push for Huang to be reinstated, in a highly unusual intervention by the government into a top company’s decision making.
“I just thought, I saw that what was happening with the company, what was happening with the stock, and I think it’s a great thing that he’s going back,” Mr. Trump said.

articles.title: Brazil’s Lula appoints private banker as Finance Minister
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Lula’s shock election win in October sent stock markets tumbling while the national currency, the real, weakened significantly
Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva has appointed private banking executive Luiz Carlos Trabuco as Finance Minister for his next term, the presidency said on Thursday (November 26, 2026).
Mr. Lula’s shock election win in October sent stock markets tumbling while the national currency, the real, weakened significantly.
The appointment of Mr. Trabuco, chairman of the board of Bradesco bank, aims to reassure the business community in Latin America’s largest economy.

“Luiz Carlos Trabuco has accepted President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva’s invitation to take the helm of the finance ministry,” the presidency stated, specifying that the banker agreed to take the job during an afternoon meeting with the Brazilian leader.
Mr. Lula will begin his fourth non-consecutive term in office in January and has so far only named one minister for that mandate.
Ahead of the official announcement, rumors circulating about Mr. Trabuco’s new job appeared to restore market confidence.
The Sao Paulo Stock Exchange was up 6% at closing on Thursday (November 26, 2026).
The national currency meanwhile regained strength after briefly crossing the symbolic threshold of six reais to the dollar on Monday.
