articles.title: Beyond 26/11: Other major terror attacks in Mumbai over the years
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Here is a look at some of the other major terror attacks that have struck Mumbai city over the years, apart from the 26/11 attacks

On November 26, 2008, 10 Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) terrorists from Pakistan arrived by sea and killed 166 people, including 18 security personnel, besides injuring more than 300 others during a 60-hour siege of Mumbai. The terrorists targeted several high-profile locations, including the Taj Mahal Palace Hotel, the Oberoi Trident, Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus and Nariman House.

But the city has been rattled by other attacks too, including the horrific 1993 Mumbai blasts. As Mumbai marks the anniversary of the 26/11 attacks, here is a look at some of the other major terror attacks that have struck the city over the years.

On March 12, 1993, 13 coordinated serial blasts ripped through Mumbai’s commercial and social hubs, killing 257 people and injuring more than 700. The city was still recovering from the communal riots of December 1992 and January 1993 that followed the demolition of the Babri Masjid on December 6, 1992, when the bombs exploded at regular intervals across Mumbai.
The attacks, the first of their kind in India, are believed to have been carried out in retaliation for the post-Babri Masjid demolition riots in Mumbai.

A month later, the Mumbai Police arrested Hindi film actor Sanjay Dutt for possessing an AK-56 rifle that was believed to be part of the arms consignment linked to the attacks. Although investigators could not establish his involvement in the conspiracy, his possession of the weapon and subsequent attempt to destroy it drew scrutiny. He was sentenced to six years in prison for illegally possessing automatic weapons linked to the consignment used in the attacks.
The alleged masterminds of the blasts, gangsters Tiger Memon and Dawood Ibrahim, remain absconding.
On March 13, 2003, a powerful explosion tore through the first-class compartment of a Karjat-bound fast local train at Mulund station, killing 11 people and injuring 82.

The attack was preceded by two other explosions. On December 6, 2002, a bomb blast at Mumbai Central railway station injured 27 people, while on January 27, 2003, a woman was killed in a blast at Vile Parle.

The first arrest was made by the Crime Branch in April 2003 when Saquib Nachan was taken into custody. Investigators later alleged that he and Lashkar-e-Taiba member Faisal Khan had masterminded the attack along with 23 others. Of the 25 accused, five, including Khan, later died.
Saquib Nachan, former general secretary of the banned Students Islamic Movement of India (SIMI), and Muzammil Ansari, along with eight others, were convicted in the case.

articles.title: India’s satellite supply chain ‘highly dependent on imports’, says space body
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: India’s space economy is currently valued at nearly $9 billion and is set to grow to $40-45 billion in less than a decade

India’s satellite supply chain is “highly dependent” on imports for critical components and the private sector’s contribution is limited to “structural assemblies” and “propulsion components” largely supplied by established public sector firms and vintage private firms, said a report by IN-SPACe, India’s regulatory-cum-promotional body for the private space sector.
While pointing out the potential of India’s private space companies, the autonomous body under the Department of Space underlined the challenges ahead.

Science Minister Jitendra Singh earlier this week said that India’s space economy is currently valued at nearly $9 billion and is set to increase to $40-45 billion in less than a decade, with the private sector set to grow from a a few startups “to nearly 400-500 companies in just a few years”.

The Supply Chain Landscape of Satellite Manufacturing in India report, which was made public on Wednesday (November 25, 2026), says that nearly 60% of satellite costs were attributed to electronic, electrical and electromechanical components, and specialised materials, many of which are imported.
India also has limited testing and certification facilities, which weakened prospects for acceptance in global markets.
Many companies largely operated on a “project-based manufacturing model”, which disincentivised long-term investment in automation and production capacity, the report noted.
Critical components often took a long time to procure – frequently 12-16 months – which led to project delays and hobbled responsiveness to market opportunities.

There was also a shortage of trained and skilled personnel in satellite systems engineering, quality assurance, testing and qualification, besides limited private-sector research and development and technology transfer.
The report was prepared by Brijesh Kumar Sol and Yudhishthir J. of IN-SPACe and “approved” by Pawan Goenka, IN-SPACe chairman.
The report isn’t a statistical survey, but paints a descriptive map of India’s satellite manufacturing supply chain.

articles.title: ECI directs states to correct erroneous entries in SIR rolls through Form 8 during ongoing Special Summary Revision
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The ECI move follows complaints of incorrect entries in several cases in the final published SIR lists

The Election Commission of India on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) directed that any incorrect or erroneous entries flagged in the electoral rolls during the ongoing Special Summary Revision (SSR) would be corrected using Form 8 after comparing the entries with the corresponding information collected during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
All the changes would be made after verification by the concerned officials and not through automated matching.
Form 8 is the ECI application for correction in voter details.
The ECI move follows complaints of incorrect entries in several cases in the final published SIR lists.
The directive was given to the Chief Electoral Officers of 25 states and UTs where the SIR has been completed and SSR is on.

The States and UTs are Andaman and Nicobar Island, Assam, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Goa, Gujarat, Kerala, Lakshadweep, Madhya Pradesh, Manipur, Puducherry, Punjab, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, West Bengal, Arunachal Pradesh, Chandigarh, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, Mizoram, Odisha, Sikkim, Karnataka and Meghalaya.
The ECI had ordered the SSR of electoral rolls with reference to January 1, 2027, as the qualifying date in these States/UTs through letters on October 15, November 4 and November 11.

In its directive on Wednesday, the poll body said: “In order to identify and rectify any probable incorrect or erroneous entries in the particulars of electors (such as name, relation name or type, date of birth, mobile number, photograph, etc.) in the existing electoral rolls during the ongoing SSR, the existing electoral particulars of the concerned electors shall be compared with the corresponding information collected during the SIR.”
“Wherever any mismatch is noticed, the same shall be flagged for verification and for taking necessary corrective action,” it said.

articles.title: Karnataka High Court quashes postal ballot tampering case against former Chikkamagaluru DC, BJP leader Jeevaraj
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The High Court of Karnataka has quashed criminal case registered in 2026 against former Chikkamagaluru Deputy Commissioner K.N. Ramesh, Returning Officer Vedamurthy T.R. and BJP leader D.N. Jeevaraj over alleged tampering of postal ballots after counting of votes in 2023 in the elections held to Sringeri Assembly constituency

The High Court of Karnataka has quashed criminal case registered in 2026 against former Chikkamagaluru Deputy Commissioner K.N. Ramesh, Returning Officer Vedamurthy T.R. and BJP leader D.N. Jeevaraja over alleged tampering of postal ballots after counting of votes in 2023 in the elections held to Sringeri Assembly constituency.

Quashing the First Information Report registered in May 2026, Justice M. Nagaprasanna ruled that the inordinate and unexplained three-year delay in registering the complaint vitiated the criminal prosecution.

The court noted that ballot boxes were sealed and locked in strong rooms under strict police security since May 13, 2023, and were opened in May 2026 following the court’s April 2026 order on Mr. Jeevaraj’s election petition challenging the legality of election of Congress candidate T.D. Raje Gowda.

The court, while partly allowing election petition on April 6, 2026, had ordered re-verification of 279 postal ballots that were rejected during counting of votes in 2023 and recount of all postal ballots if any rejected postal ballots were found to be in order during re-verification. Mr. Jeevaraj was declared elected after completion of recounting of the postal ballots on May 3, 2026. However, operation of result of recounting was subsequently stayed by the Supreme Court.

Hours after declaration of result of recounting, one Sudhir Kumar Murolli, a counting booth agent for Mr. Raje Gowda, filed the complaint alleging that a crucial document, known as “ballot paper account” sheets, was tampered with back in 2023 itself after obtaining signature of agents of all the candidates.

“If there was doubt about the counting earlier in the year 2023, nothing stopped the complainant from registering the complaint immediately thereafter. With the declaration of the results after recounting in which the candidate loses and Mr. Jeevaraj is declared as a winning candidate, investigation by the jurisdictional police on a complaint cannot emerge. It is undoubtedly hit by delay. Due to delay, there has been lot of embellishments in the complaint,” the High Court said.

articles.title: Andy Taylor, guitarist of new wave icons Duran Duran, dies at 65
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The band’s imperial stage occurred with a trio of hit albums between 1981 and 1983, with such dance-floor barnburners as ‘Girls on Film’ and ‘Union of the Snake’ and the moody ballads ‘The Chauffeur’ and ‘Save a Prayer’

Andy Taylor, the original guitarist of the 1980s English new wave band Duran Duran , whose huge pop hits include “Hungry Like the Wolf,” “The Reflex” and “Rio” and whose rise up the charts was inextricably linked to the launch of MTV, has died. He was 65.
Taylor's death was confirmed by his family and bandmates in a statement posted on social media and Duran Duran's website.

“From the moment he arrived in Birmingham from the North East with a guitar and an unshakeable belief in what we could become, he brought an indelible fire and swagger to our music. His playing drove the songs that took us around the world, and with a dry wit that was matched only by his wonderfully unsentimental, no-nonsense outlook on life, he kept us grounded and gave the band its edge through the extraordinary years that followed,” the band said.

On the night he was inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in November 2022, Taylor revealed that he had been battling stage 4 metastatic prostate cancer for several years and was unable to attend.
“I would like to thank each of my brothers in this great band,” he wrote. “You can dream about what happened to us but to experience it, on one's own terms, as mates, was beyond incredible.”

The two-time Grammy Award winners had nine gold records and six platinum ones, with 20 Top 20 singles in the U.K. and 18 in the U.S. They were two-time Ivor Novello Award winners and are MTV Video Music Award recipients.

The band's imperial stage occurred with a trio of hit albums between 1981 and 1983, with such dance-floor barnburners as “Girls on Film” and “Union of the Snake” and the moody ballads “The Chauffeur” and “Save a Prayer”. Other hits in the coming years included “The Wild Boys,” “New Moon on Monday” and “Come Undone.” Their popularity was cemented when they recorded the James Bond theme song “A View to a Kill” and earned a slot at Live Aid in 1985.

Mixing fashion, pioneering synthesisers and glam-pop swagger, the telegenic band were all over radio and young people's walls, with bassist John Taylor and singer Simon Le Bon becoming heartthrobs and the band being labelled part of the New Romantics. Princess Diana was known to be a fan, and that meant a lot to the band.

Andy Taylor, the original guitarist of the 1980s English new wave band Duran Duran , whose huge pop hits include “Hungry Like the Wolf,” “The Reflex” and “Rio” and whose rise up the charts was inextricably linked to the launch of MTV, has died. He was 65.

Taylor's death was confirmed by his family and bandmates in a statement posted on social media and Duran Duran's website.

“From the moment he arrived in Birmingham from the North East with a guitar and an unshakeable belief in what we could become, he brought an indelible fire and swagger to our music. His playing drove the songs that took us around the world, and with a dry wit that was matched only by his wonderfully unsentimental, no-nonsense outlook on life, he kept us grounded and gave the band its edge through the extraordinary years that followed,” the band said.

On the night he was inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in November 2022, Taylor revealed that he had been battling stage 4 metastatic prostate cancer for several years and was unable to attend.

“I would like to thank each of my brothers in this great band,” he wrote. “You can dream about what happened to us but to experience it, on one's own terms, as mates, was beyond incredible.”

The two-time Grammy Award winners had nine gold records and six platinum ones, with 20 Top 20 singles in the U.K. and 18 in the U.S. They were two-time Ivor Novello Award winners and are MTV Video Music Award recipients.

The band's imperial stage occurred with a trio of hit albums between 1981 and 1983, with such dance-floor barnburners as “Girls on Film” and “Union of the Snake” and the moody ballads “The Chauffeur” and “Save a Prayer”. Other hits in the coming years included “The Wild Boys,” “New Moon on Monday” and “Come Undone.” Their popularity was cemented when they recorded the James Bond theme song “A View to a Kill” and earned a slot at Live Aid in 1985.

Mixing fashion, pioneering synthesisers and glam-pop swagger, the telegenic band were all over radio and young people's walls, with bassist John Taylor and singer Simon Le Bon becoming heartthrobs and the band being labelled part of the New Romantics. Princess Diana was known to be a fan, and that meant a lot to the band.

A crash involving a fuel tanker ignited a massive fire on a major highway surrounding Cairo on Wednesday (November 25, 2026), killing at least 30 people, Egyptian authorities said.

The blaze on Ring Road, a key artery that encircles the Egyptian capital, also injured at least 25 people and left more than two dozen cars and motorcycles charred, the Public Prosecutor's office said in a statement.

Health Minister Khaled Abdel Ghaffar said the injured were taken to nearby hospitals and that he would head to the scene himself. He said the death toll was preliminary, raising concerns it could rise further.

Deadly traffic accidents claim thousands of lives every year in Egypt, which has a poor transportation safety record. Speeding, bad roads and poor enforcement of traffic laws are the main reasons behind most of the crashes.

articles.title: IAPEN summit adopts national declaration on muscle loss and sarcopenia
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The Indian Association of Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition (IAPEN), Chennai Chapter, adopted the Sarcopenia Declaration at Beyond Calories 2026, its national gastrointestinal nutrition summit organised in association with SIMS Hospitals in Chennai on November 25.

The declaration calls for early screening for sarcopenia, setting protein intake targets, regular strength exercise and early mobilisation and rehabilitation after illness, including post-intensive care follow-up.

It also emphasises professional education, India-specific research and the development of diagnostic cut-offs suited to Indian populations. It urges policymakers to include sarcopenia in national healthy-ageing and non-communicable disease programmes, particularly focusing on rural and low-income communities.

Sarcopenia is the progressive loss of muscle mass, strength and function. It can occur with ageing and is accelerated by inadequate nutrition, physical inactivity and chronic diseases. It increases the risk of falls, fractures, disability, delayed recovery from illness or surgery and loss of independence.

Doctors at the summit cited data showing that 43.6% of Indians aged 60 and above have sarcopenia, with 19.4% having its severe form. They noted that the condition also affects younger people, particularly those with chronic illnesses, poor nutrition and sedentary lifestyles.
The summit featured talks by specialists in surgical gastroenterology, critical care and nutrition.

articles.title: Modi, Shah conspiring to remove votes to regain power fourth time: Telangana CM Revanth Reddy
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Telangana Chief Minister participates in Samvidhan Raksha March held in Hyderabad

Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy alleged that the country had reached a situation where instead of the Constitution determining who should govern, those in power were attempting to decide who should be allowed to vote.

Addressing a public meeting after participating in the ‘Samvidhan Raksha March’ organised by the Telangana Pradesh Congress Committee (TPCC) on Constitution Day on Thursday (November 26, 2026), he alleged that Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union Home Minister Amit Shah were conspiring to secure a fourth consecutive term for the Bharatiiya Janata Party (BJP) at the Centre by deleting voters’ names.

The march, organised on the call of the All India Congress Committee (AICC), began at the Ambedkar statue on Tank Bund and proceeded to the Indira Gandhi statue on Necklace Road in Hyderabad. Mr. Revanth Reddy, Deputy Chief Minister Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka, TPCC president B. Mahesh Kumar Goud, AICC in-charge B.M. Sandeep, Ministers, MPs, MLAs, MLCs and senior Congress leaders participated.

Mr. Revanth Reddy said the Constitution, shaped by the vision of Mahatma Gandhi, Jawaharlal Nehru, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and B.R. Ambedkar, had provided equal voting right to all. He reminded that women in the United States were denied voting rights for several decades despite the country gaining independence much earlier, while Dr. Ambedkar had ensured universal adult franchise in India.

Mr. Revanth Reddy said the country was witnessing an ideological battle between the legacy of Mahatma Gandhi and that of Nathuram Godse. While the Gandhi family — including Sonia Gandhi, Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra — were fighting to protect the country and its Constitution, the BJP was following the legacy of Godse, he alleged.

Calling upon people to stand with the Gandhi family and the Congress, Mr. Revanth Reddy said the party that had fought for India’s independence would continue to exist for another 100 years. The BJP, which he described as a party formed for power, had no comparable history, he said.

Mr. Mahesh Kumar Goud alleged that the BJP was organising counter-rallies because it could not tolerate the public response to the Congress’s Constitution protection campaigns. He said the Congress would continue to enjoy the support of people despite such counter-mobilisations.

AICC incharge for Telangana B.M. Sandeep said the history of the Congress and that of independent India were inseparable. He alleged that the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) had played no role in the freedom struggle and that constitutional values had come under pressure over the past 13 years.

articles.title: Defence, aerospace sector outpaces IT and pharma growth in Telangana: Minister Uttam Kumar Reddy
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Telangana well positioned to emerge as a major partner in global defence and aerospace manufacturing networks, Uttam Kumar Reddy said at CII conclave in Hyderabad
The defence and aerospace sector in Telangana is growing faster than the IT and pharmaceutical sectors, according to the State’s Minister for Irrigation and Civil Supplies N. Uttam Kumar Reddy.

Production as well as exports of the defence and aerospace sector have doubled. The State is well positioned to emerge as a major partner in global defence and aerospace manufacturing networks, he said, without sharing specifics, while urging industry leaders to make the most of the emerging opportunities and the strong manufacturing ecosystem in Telangana.

A former Indian Air Force (IAF) pilot before entering politics, Mr. Reddy highlighted the prowess of the defence and aerospace sector in his address at the CII Telangana Defence and Aerospace Conclave 2026 on “Telangana to Global Markets – Building Defence and Aerospace Supply Chains,” in Hyderabad on Thursday (November 26, 2026). Recalling his days with IAF, particularly his experience of flying the MiG-23 fighter jet, the Minister said Hyderabad and Telangana were traditionally known for their strengths in the IT and pharmaceutical sectors.

Defence and aerospace manufacturing had emerged as a rapidly growing sector with immense potential for investment, exports and employment generation. The State government, as part of its Telangana Rising vision, is committed to creating a favourable environment for international companies to establish operations, expand existing facilities, undertake research and explore new business opportunities.

articles.title: Constitution Day LIVE updates: U.P. taught BJP a lesson in 2024 LS polls, silenced Modi’s ‘400 paar’ slogan: Kharge
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: PM Modi said the Constitution is a priceless heritage of Indian democracy, one that will continue to guide in realising the resolve of a developed India

Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath accused Opposition parties on Thursday (November 26, 2026) of weakening the Constitution and democratic institutions, saying those who had attempted to “strangle the Constitution” when in power were now carrying a red book to mislead people.
He criticised Congress for “disrespecting Ambedkar”, and alleged that the party did not confer the Bharat Ratna on him and conspired to prevent him from entering Parliament.

Addressing a Constitution Day programme at the Lok Bhavan auditorium in Lucknow, Mr. Adityanath said India’s sovereignty did not belong to any individual, family or particular caste but rested with the common citizens of the country.

“Those who tried to strangle the Constitution when they had the opportunity are today carrying a red book and misleading the people,” he said in an apparent attack on Congress. The chief minister also launched beautification works at 3,955 sites housing statues of Dr B R Ambedkar and other social reformers under the Dr Bhimrao Ambedkar Statue Development Scheme.

He administered a collective oath on the Preamble of the Constitution along with Deputy Chief Ministers and other dignitaries. Adityanath said 4,030 sites associated with Ambedkar and other champions of social justice had been identified across the state, of which work would begin at 3,955 locations.
The sites would be equipped with facilities such as canopies, boundary walls, CCTV cameras, security arrangements and gardens, depending on requirements, the chief minister said. -- PTI

The Union Health Ministry on Thursday (November 26, 2026) observed Constitution Day with its officers collectively reading the Preamble to the Constitution and reaffirming their commitment to its values and ideals.

The programme was held at the Kartavya Bhawan here, with senior officers, including additional secretaries, joint secretaries, directors and deputy secretaries of the Department of Health and Family Welfare, participating.

Officials from the National AIDS Control Organisation, National Health Authority and National Medical Commission, among others, joined the programme through video conferencing, the ministry said in a statement.
The observance provided an opportunity for officials to reaffirm their collective commitment to the constitutional values that guide India’s democratic framework and governance, it said. -- PTI

articles.title: Jo Bachay… government warns Netflix on Pakistani series
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: According to official sources, the government warned Netflix that the 2025 advisory banning Pakistan-origin content from streaming platforms was still in effect

The Union Ministry of Information and Broadcasting (MIB) has warned Netflix to avoid publishing any content originating in Pakistan, ahead of the December 4 launch of Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo, the country’s first series to be marketed as an original by the streaming platform.

On May 8, 2025, MIB warned streaming platforms to avoid publishing any content originating from Pakistan. “Several terrorist attacks in India have been established to have cross-border linkages with Pakistan based State and non-State actors,” that advisory said. “Recently, on 22.04.2025, the terrorist attack in Pahalgam led to the killing of several Indians, one Nepali citizen, and injuries to a number of others.”
The next month, Netflix had assured the government that it had no content from Pakistan. MIB has asked Netflix to stand by that commitment, the source said.

“In the interest of national security, all OTT platforms, media streaming platforms and intermediaries operating in India are advised to discontinue the web-series, films, songs, podcasts and other streaming media content, whether made available on a subscription based model or otherwise, having its origins in Pakistan with immediate effect,” the advisory added.

Most streaming platforms swiftly complied with the order. Post-production on Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo, as per Pakistani news reports, appeared to have concluded early last year, but no release appeared in sight following the terrorist attack in Pahalgam and the ensuing conflict between the two countries. It is unclear whether the release was pushed back globally as a result of the conflict; The Hindu reached out to Netflix and the series’ producer Momina Duraid for comment.

The series is listed on Netflix’s India catalogue with its release date, but the company has made no social media posts from its India-focused handles. The prospect of the series’ release drew condemnation from two film bodies, the All Indian Cine Workers Association (AICWA) and the Federation of Western India Cine Employees (FWICE).

According to official sources, the government warned Netflix that the 2025 advisory banning Pakistan-origin content from streaming platforms was still in effect

The Union Ministry of Information and Broadcasting (MIB) has warned Netflix to avoid publishing any content originating in Pakistan, ahead of the December 4 launch of Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo, the country’s first series to be marketed as an original by the streaming platform.

On May 8, 2025, MIB warned streaming platforms to avoid publishing any content originating from Pakistan. “Several terrorist attacks in India have been established to have cross-border linkages with Pakistan based State and non-State actors,” that advisory said. “Recently, on 22.04.2025, the terrorist attack in Pahalgam led to the killing of several Indians, one Nepali citizen, and injuries to a number of others.”

The next month, Netflix had assured the government that it had no content from Pakistan. MIB has asked Netflix to stand by that commitment, the source said.

“In the interest of national security, all OTT platforms, media streaming platforms and intermediaries operating in India are advised to discontinue the web-series, films, songs, podcasts and other streaming media content, whether made available on a subscription based model or otherwise, having its origins in Pakistan with immediate effect,” the advisory added.

Most streaming platforms swiftly complied with the order. Post-production on Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo, as per Pakistani news reports, appeared to have concluded early last year, but no release appeared in sight following the terrorist attack in Pahalgam and the ensuing conflict between the two countries. It is unclear whether the release was pushed back globally as a result of the conflict; The Hindu reached out to Netflix and the series’ producer Momina Duraid for comment.

The series is listed on Netflix’s India catalogue with its release date, but the company has made no social media posts from its India-focused handles. The prospect of the series’ release drew condemnation from two film bodies, the All Indian Cine Workers Association (AICWA) and the Federation of Western India Cine Employees (FWICE).

articles.title: Vellappally Natesan says he has ‘no differences’ with Keralam CM Satheesan
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The remarks came against the backdrop of repeated criticism and exchanges between Natesan and Satheesan before UDF came to power following Assembly election earlier this year

Sree Narayana Dharma Paripalana (SNDP) Yogam general secretary Vellappally Natesan on Thursday said he had “no differences” with Keralam Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan, signalling a softening of his stand towards the Congress leader after a series of public exchanges between them.
The SNDP Yogam represents the numerically strong Ezhava community in Keralam.

Speaking to reporters, Mr. Natesan said there had been no differences between him and Mr. Satheesan. “There are no differences with me in the first place. So, why should we talk about reconciliation,” he asked.
The remarks came against the backdrop of repeated criticism and exchanges between Mr. Natesan and Mr. Satheesan before the UDF came to power following the Assembly election earlier this year.
Asked about his past criticism of Mr. Satheesan, Mr. Natesan said there was no difference in his assessment of the Congress leader “then and now.”
“I have only expressed my views on specific issues,” he said.
Mr. Natesan said he had criticised Mr. Satheesan for “an immature stand” and for not respecting the Opposition when the latter was the Leader of the Opposition during the previous government.
When asked whether Mr. Satheesan has matured since becoming the Chief Minister, he said: “It is only six months. Let’s wait and see.”

Mr. Natesan said it was Nair Service Society (NSS) general secretary G. Sukumaran Nair who had earlier announced that Mr. Satheesan would not be allowed into the organisation’s office, adding that he had never objected to the Chief Minister visiting the SNDP premises.
“I have never objected to anyone coming here. It was the NSS leadership that announced such a restriction,” he said.

fullParagraphs: Flames rose high above the site, followed by black smoke that swept across the Thai capital’s skyline

A major fire broke out at Thailand’s Bangchak Corp’s Phra Khanong oil refinery in the capital, Bangkok, on Thursday (November 26, 2026), leaving at least seven people injured, four of those seriously, according to the city’s Erawan Emergency Medical Centre.

The company said it has ‌shut down all production ​units following the ‌fire, and later released a statement saying that the fire at its Bangkok oil refinery was “under control”. The company added that the cause of the incident was being investigated

A fire broke out at ‌the facility around ‌2.45 ⁠p.m. (local time) and was ⁠brought under control and extinguished around 30 minutes later, the ​company ‌said in a statement. The refinery has a maximum ​capacity of 1,20,000 barrels per day.
Thai energy conglomerate Bangchak operates two refineries, ⁠including the Phra Khanong facility, with ⁠a combined refining capacity of about 3,00,000 ‌barrels per day.
AFP reporters a few kilometres away said the blast shook their doors. Flames rose high above the site, followed by black smoke that swept across the Thai capital’s skyline.

articles.title: Situation in India-China border areas remain ‘generally stable’, says China
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: On November 24, 2026, India and China concluded a second round of Corps Commander-level talks aimed at easing tensions along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) in Arunachal Pradesh

The situation in the India-China border areas remain “generally stable”, China’s Defence Ministry spokesperson and PLA Senior Colonel Chen Xi said on Thursday (November 26, 2026) adding that China “does not recognize the so-called Arunachal Pradesh illegally set up by India.”

“China and India maintain communication through diplomatic and military channels, including general-level talks, to jointly implement the consensus reached by the two sides and safeguard peace and tranquility in the border areas”, he said in response to a question at a press briefing on recent tensions in the Eastern sector of the border, Chinese state media reported.

On November 24, 2026, India and China concluded a second round of Corps Commander-level talks aimed at easing tensions along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) in Arunachal Pradesh and putting in place measures to prevent friction between troops deployed along the frontier ahead of the onset of harsh winter conditions.

Sources in the Ministry of Defence confirmed that the closely guarded discussions, which began on November 8, 2026, a day after Deepavali, continued for nearly 10 days, with a short break in between. The talks were described as cordial, though it remains unclear whether the measures discussed will be implemented on the ground before winter sets in fully.

The latest round of talks primarily focused on establishing engagement protocols between the two sides, preventing face-offs and misunderstandings between troops deployed along the frontier, maintaining open communication channels and reducing tensions in the eastern sector. Both countries have deployed substantial numbers of troops in the region.

articles.title: Sheikh Hasina’s return gambit tests Bangladesh’s political fault lines
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The ousted leader’s December 16 return plan has energised the Awami League leaders and cadre, tested Tarique Rahman’s government and complicated Dhaka’s efforts to reset ties with New Delhi

Mahmud Tanzid, a 27-year-old private-sector employee in Dhaka, has postponed a trip he had planned for the first week of December. After weeks of unrest, particularly in Gopalganj, and with former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina announcing her intention to return to Bangladesh on December 16, he fears the situation could deteriorate further. He is no longer certain what the coming weeks will bring as Ms. Hasina’s Awami League has already called a nationwide lockdown on November 29-30.

Whether Ms. Hasina actually lands in Dhaka on December 16 or not, she has already reshaped Bangladesh’s political calendar. Her announcement has turned the countdown to Victory Day, which marks the end of the nine-month Liberation War in 1971 and the official surrender of Pakistani forces to the joint command of Bangladeshi and Indian forces, into a test of political will.

The 79-year-old former Prime Minister intends to end more than two years of exile in India on Victory Day. It is the first time she has specified a date for her return. In doing so, the Awami League, which was banned by the post-Hasina interim administration, has transformed what began as a localised law-and-order crisis into a national contest over political legitimacy.

The Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) government’s response has been uncompromising. State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humayun Kobir said Ms. Hasina could return only through extradition, effectively “in handcuffs”. Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed reiterated the government’s position on Wednesday (November 25), saying “a convicted fugitive” could return only through the extradition process.

Dismissing the shifting deadlines — initially November, then December, and now December 16 — Mr. Ahmed said the government felt “no worry or pressure” and that law enforcement agencies remained on constant alert. He warned that the Awami League would face strict legal action if it resorted to militancy, arson or attacks on people and property.

articles.title: Vivo launches X500 Pro Max, X500 and X500 along with Watch GT2
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The Chinese smartphone maker also launched its first smartwatch, Vivo Watch GT2, in India having a 2.07 inch display, with up to 25-day claimed battery life

Vivo on Thursday (November 26, 2026) launched new smartphones under its super-premium X series , featuring Vivo X500 Pro Max, X500 Pro and X500. The camera-centric phones succeed the X300 series, and bring ZEISS-tuned lenses and OriginOS 7 out of the box.
The Chinese smartphone maker also launched its first smartwatch, Vivo Watch GT2, in India having a 2.07 inch display, with up to 25-day claimed battery life. The Vivo Watch GT2 costs ₹14,999.
Vivo X500 Pro Max has a 6.85 inch flat LTPO AMOLED display, with up to 144Hz refresh rate and 5,000 nits peak brightness.
Vivo X500 Pro Max ships with a 7,800 mAh battery supported by a 90W wired charger and a 40W wireless charging support. It is IP68 and IP69 rated for dust and water resistance.

Vivo X500 Pro Max runs on MediaTek Dimensity 9600 Pro chipset with up to 12 GB RAM and 512 GB storage. It operates on OriginOS 7 based on Android 17 out of the box. The phone will get 7 years of OS and security patches.
The Vivo X500 Pro Max sports a 50 MP main camera, a 200 MP telephoto camera and a 50 MP ultrawide lens. It has a 50 MP front camera.
Vivo X500 Pro Max comes in Apex Orange and Eternal Black. It starts at ₹1,64,999 (12GB/256GB) and ₹1,79,999 (12GB/512GB). The sale begins December 3.
Vivo X500 Pro get a 6.36 inch flat LTPO AMOLED display, with up to 144Hz refresh rate and 5,000 nits peak brightness.
Vivo X500 Pro uses a 6,510 mAh battery with a 90W wired and 40W wireless charging support.
Vivo X500 Pro also features MediaTek Dimensity 9600 Pro with up to 12 GB RAM and 256 GB storage. It too operates on OriginOS 7.

articles.title: Apple to open first store in Hyderabad on December 10
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Apple Kukatpally opens Thursday, December 10 at 5 PM, the iPhone-maker announced
Apple is gearing up to open its first store, Apple Kukatpally, located at Lake Shore-Y Junction Mall in Hyderabad, on December 10.
The new store is Apple’s seventh in the country, as the premium gadget-maker grows its retail presence in India by targeting its largest cities.
Customers will be able to experience and buy Apple products, apart from accessing services and support directly, the company highlighted.
Hyderabad houses Apple’s Research and Development and Retail Customer Care teams.
The design language for Apple Kukatpally takes inspiration from pearls, in a nod to Hyderabad’s identity and historical legacy as the ‘City of Pearls.’

The iPhone-maker’s other retail locations in India include Apple BKC and Apple Borivali in Mumbai, Apple Saket and Apple Noida in Delhi NCR, Apple Hebbal in Bengaluru, and Apple Koregaon Park in Pune.

“Ahead of opening day, customers are invited to download exclusive Apple Kukatpally wallpapers and stickers, explore a curated Apple Music playlist inspired by the sounds of Hyderabad, and learn more about the upcoming store at apple.com/in/retail/kukatpally,” announced Apple in a press release.

articles.title: Meet the little stint: The tiny Siberian traveller visiting India’s wetlands
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The Little Stint travels thousands of kilometres between its Arctic breeding grounds and Indian wetlands. But as shrinking mudflats and changing landscapes threaten its feeding and resting habitats, this tiny shorebird tells an important story about conserving wetlands

The little stint, a 25-gram shorebird, comes in lakhs from the Arctic to the shores of India, particularly to Point Calimere. “It’s an unforgettable sight,” says S Sivakumar, who has been involved in monitoring shorebirds in the Gulf of Mannar for over a decade. The birds remain through the winter months and depart between March and April, sometimes later in May. “In the 1980s, the little stint could be seen in several lakhs at any point of time. Even now, the numbers are still over a lakh as the Point Calimere Wetland Complex covers over 300 kilometres across coastal Tamil Nadu ,” says Sivakumar, assistant director at the Bombay Natural History Society’s Bird Migration Study Centre at Point Calimere, adding that such long-term observations help scientists understand how bird populations and their habitats are changing.
The birds remain through the winter months and depart between March and April, sometimes later in May | Photo Credit: S Sivakumar

The tiny bird’s annual migration journey, a feat of endurance, involves multiple stopovers across different landscapes, each of which must provide sufficient food and safe resting grounds. As shrinking mudflats and changing landscapes threaten its feeding and resting habitats, this tiny shorebird tells an important story about conserving wetlands.

Ashvin Viswanathan, scientist at Bird Count India , places the little stints as the most visible representatives of a special group of shorebirds that breed in the Arctic. “ This group is declining rapidly due to climate change and loss of habitat. Little stints too are declining in India according to SoIB,” he says, referring to the State of India’s Birds assessment. Their widespread presence, he adds, indicates the health of wetland ecosystems in India as well as conditions in the Arctic. The fact that the little stint is still a fairly common bird does not mean that it is beyond risk. It’s numbers and distribution can help draw attention to changes taking place across the habitats it depends on.
The numbers are still over a lakh at Point Calimere wetlands | Photo Credit: S Sivakumar

The bird’s preparation for migration is as fascinating as the journey itself which begins from a landscape that includes Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, the Caspian Sea and Tibet, before reaching the wintering grounds, the lagoons, islands and mudflats of the Gulf of Mannar. As temperatures drop in the Arctic and the food becomes scarce, it triggers the bird to move towards warmer regions. “Before setting off, they enter a phase of intense feeding called hyperphagia. They feed voraciously to build up fat reserves that act as fuel during its journey. This can add 50 to 75 percent to the bird’s body weight. There are also physiological changes, some organs shrink in size as the bird prepares for the demands of sustained flight,” explains Sivakumar adding that India is an important destination along the Central Asian Flyway that connects the bird with wintering habitats further South. The birds can be found along several coastal wetlands, including Point Calimere, Pulicat, parts of Puducherry and Kanyakumari, the Sundarbans, and the mudflats of Gujarat and Maharashtra. Across Tamil Nadu, the species is familiar to birders. “You can spot them at wetlands such as Kurichi and Ukkadam in Coimbatore,” says birder K Selvaganesh adding that the flock plays an important part of the food chain as prey for raptors, including the Western marsh marrier and the brahminy kite.

Goa-based Rakesh Dhareshwar, a wildlife photographer says Goa and the wider west coast are reliable places to find them each season. “This year, I was delighted to see them inland too, at Bhigwan in Maharashtra, during a mid-Novemeber trip. However, shorebirds worldwide are in decline. Loss of coastal and inland wetlands, reclamation of mudflats, and pollution threaten stopover and wintering sites these birds depend on. The good news is that we can fix this. Protecting wetlands, salt pans and estuaries, and sharing spaces thoughtfully with people can make a real difference.”
Shorebirds worldwide are in decline | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement

In his new book, Little Stint: A Migrant’s Tale (Neythal Pathipakam), author Byju H explores the bird’s remarkable journey through a blend of science and unconventional storytelling allowing the bird to narrate its own life, beginning with emerging from an egg in the Arctic tundra. “I wanted readers to travel with the bird,” he says adding that the book also highlights the fact that the bird’s ability to navigate vast distances depends on the availability of suitable wetlands along its migratory route.
File photo of little stints and kentish plovers | Photo Credit: PRINCE FREDERICK

articles.title: India’s defence start-up boom is outrunning its talent pipeline
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Without targeted skilling, 40-45% of roles in the sector could remain unfilled by 2030, a gap that risks bottlenecking aircraft development, unmanned systems, naval projects and secure communications networks

2026 has proven to be the best year on record for India’s defence manufacturing sector, with the annual defence production reaching an all-time high of ₹1.78 lakh crore in FY 2025-26. Defence exports reached a record ₹38,424 crore in FY 2025-26, which is 62.66% higher than ₹23,622 crore the previous year, with Indian-made equipment now being exported to more than 80 countries.

Indigenous defence production has quadrupled, rising from ₹46,429 crore in FY 2014-15 to ₹1.78 lakh crore in 2025. The government has set its sights on ₹3 lakh crore in annual defence production and ₹50,000 crore in exports by 2029, alongside achieving roughly 88% self-sufficiency in ammunition production. Moreover, the share of the private industry is also expanding rapidly. Its contribution increased to 24% of total output (around ₹42,000 crore) in FY 2025-26, up from 22% the previous year.

Behind the headline numbers lies a more contested story: whether India has a sufficiently trained workforce to sustain this growth, and whether the engineering colleges, and State-run startup schemes can actually support this development. Interviews with founders, a former Navy officer-turned-entrepreneur, a materials science executive and an academic administrator suggest the sector’s talent problem is not a shortage of engineers, it is a shortage of engineers who understand what happens when a prototype has to survive a battlefield.

India’s defence technology market alone, was valued at $7.6 billion in 2025 and is projected to reach $19 billion by 2030 according to a private industry report by staffing firm Quess Corp. By 2030, technology-led systems are expected to make up almost half of India’s overall defence market, marking what the report calls a shift “from platform-driven development to advanced engineering and digital capability building”.

The same report flags a structural problem: specialised roles in radar engineering, RF engineering, avionics, propulsion, optical engineering, quantum communications, systems integration, test and validation, and certification currently account for less than 5% of the existing defence workforce. Without targeted skilling, the report warns, 40-45% of these roles could remain unfilled by 2030, a gap that risks bottlenecking aircraft development, unmanned systems, naval projects and secure communications networks.

articles.title: Experts say new U.S. tariffs do not pose substantial threat, India should not rush into trade deal
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: The latest proposal by the USTR takes the tariff framework on India back to what it was at the start of trade deal negotiations

The new 25% tariffs proposed by the U.S. on India do not pose a substantial risk to Indian exports, and India should go ahead with a trade deal only if it is balanced and reciprocal, according to exporters and trade and tariff experts.

An analysis of India’s trade relationship with the U.S. over the last two years showed that the latest tariffs announced by the U.S. have returned the tariff relationship to where it was at the start of trade deal negotiations.
The Office of the U.S. Trade Representative on Wednesday proposed a net tariff of 25% on goods imported from India, which could be reduced to 17% if a trade deal is signed by the two countries.

The proposed 25% tariff is nearly the same as the 26% tariff U.S. President Donald Trump had originally proposed in his ‘Liberation Day’ reciprocal tariff measure in April 2025. A week later, Mr. Trump paused these tariffs in a bid to secure trade deals with other countries.

In July 2025, he announced a 25% tariff on India, the same as what the USTR is now proposing. But Mr. Trump soon announced an additional 25% tariff as a penalty for India’s Russian oil imports taking the total tariff on Indian goods to 50%.

During that time, Mr. Trump also announced a 50% tariff on the import of steel and aluminium from all countries. The latest tariffs by the USTR are not in addition to those tariffs, meaning Indian steel and aluminium will continue to attract a 50% duty.

In February 2026, India and the U.S. issued a joint statement announcing the framework for an interim deal on trade, under which the U.S. would reduce its tariffs on Indian goods to 18%. This is very close to the 17% the U.S. is proposing now, should a deal be signed, nearly 10 months after the joint statement was issued.
As such, the pre-deal, post-deal, and steel and aluminium tariffs by the U.S. on India largely remain where they were at the start of negotiations.
Exporters and trade experts have said that India should proceed with a trade deal only if it satisfies Indian interests.

“FIEO supports the government’s efforts to conclude the Bilateral Trade Agreement at an early date,” said S.C. Ralhan, president of the Federation of Indian Export Organisations. “The agreement should be balanced and reciprocal, safeguard India’s long-term economic and developmental interests, and ensure that Indian exporters can compete on a level-playing field with suppliers from other countries in the U.S. market.”

Medics said an Israeli airstrike hit an apartment in Deir Al-Balah in central Gaza Strip on Thursday, killing ‌Khaled Abu Nada, the deputy Gaza education minister, and his wife.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the attack was one of ‌a series of targeted killings carried out recently against members and ‌senior ⁠officials in Hamas, adding that Israel has killed about 80 ⁠Hamas militants in the past month.
"No terrorist is immune, and no one in the Hamas leadership will manage to evade us," said Mr. Netanyahu.

The Israeli military said Abu Nada oversaw ​Hamas' economic portfolio and managed its ‌banking and investment network, directing funds toward militant activities and force buildup. The military said his death may weaken the group's ability to sustain its finances and support its military capabilities. Hamas confirmed the death but had ‌no immediate comment on the allegations about his role.

Two other separate ​airstrikes killed six people in Tuffah neighbourhood and Beach refugee camp overnight in Gaza City, medics added. Later on Thursday (November 26, 2026), ⁠medics said Israeli gunfire killed a 62-year-old man in eastern Bureij refugee camp.
The Israeli military didn't immediately comment on those seven reported deaths.

Israel has continued to ‌carry out attacks that it says target Hamas but which have also killed many civilians. The broader ceasefire plan, backed by U.S. President Donald Trump, has not halted the violence or secured Hamas' disarmament.
Abu Nada was the third senior Hamas official Israel has killed since Tuesday, after two senior security officials.

articles.title: Nvidia stops shipping AI servers to four Southeast Asian nations
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The Financial Times report said Nvidia had instructed manufacturing partners to stop shipping computer servers to buyers in Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia

U.S. tech titan Nvidia is not allowing orders of computer servers containing its artificial intelligence chips to be shipped to four Southeast Asian countries, the Financial Times reported Thursday (November 26, 2026).

The article comes after Washington tightened export controls for the sensitive components in the wake of an espionage scandal that has engulfed Nvidia, forcing out longtime CEO Jensen Huang before his reinstatement on Sunday (November 22, 2026).
Citing national security concerns, the United States has since 2022 restricted export to tech rival China of Nvidia's industry-leading advanced chips that are used to train and run AI tools.

Washington last week moved to close a loophole in those controls, to crack down on chip smuggling, but also the large grey market of Chinese companies renting computing power from data centres in third countries, often in Southeast Asia.
The Financial Times report said Nvidia had instructed manufacturing partners to stop shipping computer servers to buyers in Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia.
The British newspaper, citing three people with knowledge of the matter, said it was unclear whether the halt was temporary.
What are AI PCs that Nvidia's Jensen Huang is betting on?
Nvidia's web of AI bets: smart strategy or bubble risk?
It named U.S. giants Dell and Supermicro, who package Nvidia AI chips into servers for data centres, as two affected partners.

Buyers affected include Singapore-based cloud computing company Aolani, which had planned to provide access to the Nvidia hardware to Chinese TikTok owner ByteDance through leasing agreements, the Financial Times said.

articles.title: Myanmar says it will not fully comply with ICJ genocide orders
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The ruling by ‌the ⁠ICJ, the first instance of the UN court holding a ⁠state responsible for genocide, is final but the court has very limited options to enforce it

Myanmar's military-backed ‌President has said his administration will not comply with all ​measures ordered by the UN's top court, which last ⁠week ruled that the country's security forces had committed genocide against the Rohingya.

The International Court of Justice (ICJ) found that the Myanmar military's actions against the mainly ‌Muslim Rohingya minority in 2017, including thousands of killings, the burning of hundreds of villages and widespread sexual violence, amounted ‌to genocide — and ordered a slew of measures.
The ruling by ‌the ⁠ICJ, the first instance of the UN court holding a ⁠state responsible for genocide, is final but the court has very limited options to enforce it.
"Myanmar would take actions appropriate for a responsible country but would not comply with requirements it considered inappropriate," he said in a meeting on ‌Wednesday, according to state media.
Min Aung Hlaing did not elaborate ​on what court orders his administration considered inappropriate.

The ICJ has ordered Myanmar to end ongoing breaches of the Genocide ⁠Convention and promptly investigate, prosecute and punish people reasonably suspected of involvement in the 2017 military operations. It also ordered the country to provide guarantees ‌that such violations will not be repeated.

Myanmar must also facilitate the return of displaced Rohingya, restore or replace lost property, help locate missing people, provide rehabilitation to survivors, and protect Rohingya from discrimination and persecution.
The court further ordered Myanmar to pay compensation for the harm caused to Rohingya that is not remedied through restitution.
Myanmar must report ‌back within two years on the measures it has taken, including proposed compensation, ​the order said.
Myanmar has maintained that operations undertaken by its security forces in northern Rakhine state during 2016–2018 ⁠were counter-terrorism actions against an insurgent group.

articles.title: Delhi tops list of most polluted NCR cities for PM2.5, PM10 despite no severe AQI days
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The city's air quality remained in the poor or very poor categories for 30 days

Delhi topped the list of the 10 most polluted cities in the National Capital Region for both PM2.5 and PM10 during the October 1-November 25 period this year, moving up from third and fourth positions in the corresponding period last year.

According to an analysis of India Air Quality Portal by EnviroCatalysts, Delhi recorded an average PM2.5 concentration of 113 micrograms per cubic metre during the period, followed by Gurugram at 109, Noida at 105, Ghaziabad at 103, Meerut at 96, Baghpat and Greater Noida at 95, Panipat at 90, Bulandshahr at 82, and Faridabad at 69.
For PM10, Delhi again topped the list with an average concentration of 221 micrograms per cubic metre.
Gurugram recorded 207, followed by Bulandshahr at 201, Noida at 200, Ghaziabad at 197, Baghpat at 193, Greater Noida at 192, Meerut at 178, and Panipat and Faridabad at 173 each.

In the corresponding period last year, Delhi recorded an average PM2.5 concentration of 158 micrograms per cubic metre, ranking third behind Ghaziabad and Noida. Its average PM10 concentration stood at 287 micrograms per cubic metre, placing it fourth behind Ghaziabad, Noida and Greater Noida. Ghaziabad topped both lists in 2025.

A comparison of the same period over the last six years, from 2021 to 2026, shows that Delhi topped the PM2.5 list three times, in 2022, 2024 and 2026, while it recorded the highest average PM10 concentration twice, in 2024 and 2026.

Despite topping both pollution charts, Delhi did not record a single day in the severe air quality category during the 56 days. It recorded three days in the satisfactory category, 23 in moderate, 18 in poor and 12 in very poor.

"Air across the NCR has been clearly better this season, helped by good October rain and less pollution reaching Delhi from spread-out and fewer farm fires. The next step is to cut year-round sources such as vehicles, dust and waste burning across the whole region, so this improvement becomes the new normal," Sunil Dahiya, founder and lead analyst at EnviroCatalyst, told PTI.
The city's air quality remained in the poor or very poor categories for 30 days.

In 2025, Delhi recorded four satisfactory days, nine moderate days, 13 poor days, 27 very poor days and three severe days. The previous year, air quality remained in the moderate category for 13 days, poor for 10 days, very poor for 25 days and severe for eight days.

articles.title: Mindfulness linked to healthier social media use, better mental health: study
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The findings showed that higher levels of mindfulness were associated with lower levels of depression, anxiety, stress, loneliness and fear of missing out (FoMO)

People with higher levels of mindfulness are more likely to have healthier social media habits and better mental health outcomes, according to a review of 43 studies involving more than 28,000 participants.
Mindfulness involves observing one’s thoughts and feelings without judgement.

Researchers led by University College London analysed the studies and found that people who reported being more mindful in their daily lives were more likely to report healthier patterns of social media use.

The findings, published in the journal PLOS One , also showed that higher levels of mindfulness were associated with lower levels of depression, anxiety, stress, loneliness and fear of missing out (FoMO).
Previous studies have shown that cultivating mindfulness through practices such as meditation or mindfulness-based therapy can help reduce symptoms of stress, anxiety and depression.
The review contributes to the debate over whether social media use poses a risk to mental health or aggravates existing mental health problems, the researchers said.

Lead author Dr Marc S Tibber from University College London’s Division of Psychology and Language Sciences said the findings supported a shift away from simplistic questions about whether social media was inherently good or bad.

“Our findings support a move away from reductive questions about whether social media is inherently good or bad, towards an exploration of how complex interactions between individuals, technologies, and the broader social contexts in which they are embedded shape both the potential benefits and harms of social media for mental health,” Tibber said.

The review suggested that mindfulness may play a protective role, he said, adding that it could be a potential target for interventions aimed at promoting healthier digital engagement, although further research was needed.
The studies included participants aged 10 to 92, with university students accounting for the largest group at 46.5 %.

The findings showed that higher levels of mindfulness were associated with lower levels of depression, anxiety, stress, loneliness and fear of missing out (FoMO)

People with higher levels of mindfulness are more likely to have healthier social media habits and better mental health outcomes, according to a review of 43 studies involving more than 28,000 participants.

Mindfulness involves observing one’s thoughts and feelings without judgement.

Researchers led by University College London analysed the studies and found that people who reported being more mindful in their daily lives were more likely to report healthier patterns of social media use.

The findings, published in the journal PLOS One , also showed that higher levels of mindfulness were associated with lower levels of depression, anxiety, stress, loneliness and fear of missing out (FoMO).

Previous studies have shown that cultivating mindfulness through practices such as meditation or mindfulness-based therapy can help reduce symptoms of stress, anxiety and depression.

The review contributes to the debate over whether social media use poses a risk to mental health or aggravates existing mental health problems, the researchers said.

Lead author Dr Marc S Tibber from University College London’s Division of Psychology and Language Sciences said the findings supported a shift away from simplistic questions about whether social media was inherently good or bad.

“Our findings support a move away from reductive questions about whether social media is inherently good or bad, towards an exploration of how complex interactions between individuals, technologies, and the broader social contexts in which they are embedded shape both the potential benefits and harms of social media for mental health,” Tibber said.

The review suggested that mindfulness may play a protective role, he said, adding that it could be a potential target for interventions aimed at promoting healthier digital engagement, although further research was needed.

The studies included participants aged 10 to 92, with university students accounting for the largest group at 46.5 %.

articles.title: Infectious diseases from free-ranging domestic animals threaten Nilgiris wildlife
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Five of the 12 reported instances of wildlife deaths since 2005 likely due to infections contracted from feral animals were recorded in the Nilgiris district, shows report by Forest Department
Frequent interactions between wildlife and free-ranging domestic animals raise concerns about disease transmission to wildlife in the Nilgiris.

According to a report submitted by the Forest Department to the Madras High Court, five of the 12 reported instances of infections that caused wildlife deaths, likely due to interactions with feral animals, since 2005 were recorded in the Nilgiris district.
Necropsy on wildlife carcasses had found canine distemper and rabies as the cause of deaths, which had been reported in the Nilgiris, Gudalur and Mudumalai Tiger Reserve (MTR) forest divisions.

S. Muralidharan, who is appearing as the party-in-person before the High Court, has sought judicial intervention to address the threat to wildlife. He told The Hindu that there have been instances of diseases such as canine distemper and rabies spreading to wildlife from free-ranging domestic animals, particularly dogs.

He pointed out that such diseases had threatened the survival of vulnerable wildlife populations, citing outbreaks of canine distemper among Asiatic lions in Gujarat as an example of the potential consequences. “This is a very serious concern, especially in areas where there is a very high interface between wildlife and human communities, which feed and maintain free-ranging dog populations, like in the Nilgiris” he said.

Mr. Muralidharan called on the government to take measures to manage free-ranging dogs and cats in areas bordering tiger reserves and reserve forests across the State, including their removal from these areas to protect wildlife.
“These animals also hunt small game such as birds and even deer and can be extremely aggressive,” he said.

According to the report filed by the Forest Department, the deaths of the 12 animals reported due to transmission of disease from domestic animals include those of leopards (canine distemper), Nilgiri langur (rabies), Indian gaur (rabies), sloth bear (rabies and ehrlichiosis) and golden jackals (canine distemper and parvovirus infection).

Conservationists said that the number of animals dying from diseases transmitted to wildlife from feral animals could be much higher as not all wildlife deaths are reported or are noticed if they occur inside reserve forests.

The deaths had been reported in Kodaikanal, Kalakkad Mundanthurai Tiger Reserve (KMTR), Sivaganga, Theni, Kanniyakumari and Tirunelveli, but the Nilgiris had the highest number of the reported deaths.

articles.title: Training vs inference: What’s the distinction at the heart of the Sarvam AI-China models controversy? | Explained
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Can India build an indigenous AI ecosystem while hosting models developed in China? What is Sarvam’s Token Factory? What does it mean for India’s AI ambitions?

The story so far: Sarvam AI has so far been known for developing its own Artificial Intelligence (AI) models with support from the government’s IndiaAI Mission . On November 16, the Bengaluru-based startup added another part to its business with the launch of Token Factory, a commercial service that gives businesses access to its own models and those developed by other companies, including Chinese firms.

The launch prompted a debate over whether offering Chinese-developed models through a commercial platform aligns with India’s ambition to build indigenous AI capabilities, particularly when a company has received government support.

Hemant Mohapatra, partner at Lightspeed India and an investor in Sarvam, defended the commercial rationale. In a November 18 post on X, he said global AI companies were generating substantial revenue by hosting models, including Chinese ones, on infrastructure in India and serving customers worldwide. He attributed the opportunity to a global shortage of GPUs, which has made computing capacity in India attractive to companies seeking to run their models.

On November 22, Sarvam co-founder Pratyush Kumar issued a clarification on X, addressing questions about the company’s government support, its decision to host foreign-developed models and its commitment to developing its own models. He said Sarvam had used subsidised computing access under the IndiaAI Mission to train its 105B model, while maintaining that its inference business did not conflict with its objective of developing its own models.

The government has also defended Sarvam’s commercial strategy. IT Secretary S Krishnan told reporters that the Centre did not see any misuse of IndiaAI Mission support in the company’s decision to offer foreign-developed models through Token Factory. “Based on what Sarvam has told us, based on the experience that people have, we do not see any misuse of the support, which the IndiaAI Mission has provided to Sarvam in the service that they are now offering,” he said. Krishnan said there was no contradiction between developing indigenous models and offering foreign-developed ones commercially, adding that AI companies also needed a revenue model.
Token Factory is an inference platform that allows developers and businesses to access several AI models through a single Application Programming Interface (API).

An API allows one software application to communicate with another. Instead of setting up and managing the infrastructure needed to run a model, a business can connect its software to Sarvam’s API and send requests to the model it wants to use.

The platform offers Sarvam’s 105-billion-parameter model, alongside open-weight models such as GLM 5.3 and GLM 5.3 Flash from China’s Z.ai, DeepSeek V4 models from DeepSeek, Kimi models from Moonshot AI, and Google’s Gemma 4 31B.
Open-weight models are those whose trained parameters, or weights, are made available for others to download and run. Businesses can use them without having to develop the models from scratch.
Sarvam says Token Factory runs the models on GPU clusters located in India. Customers pay according to the number of tokens processed.

articles.title: Two-thirds of adolescents in India are deficient in vitamin B12: ICMR survey
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Findings raise concerns about the long-term consequences of nutritional deficiencies across generations, particularly among children, adolescents, and pregnant women

Nearly two-thirds of Indian adolescents are deficient in vitamin B12, a micronutrient essential for brain development, healthy nerve function, and the formation of red blood cells, according to a new national survey by the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR).
The findings raise concerns about the long-term consequences of nutritional deficiencies across generations, particularly among children, adolescents, and pregnant women.

The Survey for Assessment of Markers of Population Health, Activity, Diet and Anthropometry (SAMPADA), conducted by ICMR’s National Institute of Nutrition during 2023–25, found vitamin B12 deficiency in 66.1% of adolescent boys and 65.4% of adolescent girls. The prevalence was 63.1% among pregnant women, 60.4% among adult men aged 20–59, and 57.4% among women aged 15–49. Even among children aged five to nine, 46.5% were deficient.

The survey, which analysed over 1.7 lakh blood samples from a population of more than two lakh people across 183 districts and 35 States and Union Territories, defined deficiency as serum vitamin B12 levels below 203 pg/mL.

Vitamin B12 plays a critical role in DNA synthesis, red blood cell formation, and maintenance of the protective covering around nerves. Prolonged deficiency can cause peripheral neuropathy, impaired balance, memory problems, and, in severe cases, irreversible neurological damage. In infants, severe deficiency can result in developmental delays and neurological impairment.

“Research conducted in Pune over the past three decades has shown that vitamin B12 deficiency is common among adolescents and women of reproductive age, with important implications for the health of future generations. Low maternal B12 status, particularly when accompanied by high folate levels, has been associated with increased fat accumulation and insulin resistance in children, potentially predisposing them to diabetes and other non-communicable diseases later in life. These effects are believed to be linked to epigenetic programming arising from nutritional imbalances before conception and during pregnancy,’’ said Chittaranjan Yajnik, director, Diabetes Unit, KEM Hospital, Pune.

He added that India must move beyond an exclusive focus on iron and folic acid and consider including physiological doses of B12 in supplementation programmes for women, alongside carefully planned food fortification, improved nutrition literacy among adolescents, particularly girls, and the generation of robust, India-specific evidence to establish appropriate nutritional requirements and interventions.

The findings are particularly significant for maternal and child health, with nearly two-thirds of pregnant women showing a deficiency. Low maternal B12 levels have been associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes, including neural tube defects and low birth weight, as well as poorer offspring developmental outcomes.

Vitamin B12 is found naturally in foods such as meat, fish, eggs, and dairy products. Inadequate dietary intake, particularly among people consuming predominantly plant-based diets, and impaired absorption can contribute to deficiency.

The findings also raise questions about whether India’s nutrition programmes are adequately addressing deficiencies beyond iron and folic acid. The Anemia Mukt Bharat strategy focuses substantially on iron and folic acid supplementation, testing and treatment of anaemia, deworming, and food fortification. Although fortified rice includes vitamin B12, routine B12 screening and supplementation are not central components of the programme.

articles.title: Indian pharma company Hetero begins supply of generic twice-yearly HIV prevention injection in Africa
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The World Health Organization (WHO) has recommended twice-yearly injectable lenacapavir as an additional HIV prevention option, based on clinical evidence showing high efficacy in preventing HIV infection

Hyderabad-based pharmaceutical company Hetero has begun phased shipments of generic injectable lenacapavir, a long-acting drug for HIV prevention, to three African countries. The company plans to supply 300,000 vials initially to Zambia, Uganda and Zimbabwe.
Lenacapavir is used as pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) to reduce the risk of acquiring HIV. Unlike daily oral PrEP medicines, the injectable formulation is administered once every six months.

Hetero is launching the generic drug under the brand names Lexapir and Capvic. The company expects to introduce its generic oral initiation tablets by January 2027. These tablets form part of the PrEP regimen and will be supplied by the original manufacturer, Gilead Sciences, in the interim.

The launch follows Gilead’s non-exclusive voluntary licensing agreements with six generic manufacturers, allowing them to manufacture and supply generic lenacapavir in 120 eligible countries. The licensing arrangement is intended to expand access to the drug in low- and middle-income countries.

Hetero said its generic injectable formulation and oral initiation tablets had received an Expert Review Panel recommendation, allowing eligible procurement through applicable Global Fund channels while regulatory approval or WHO prequalification processes continue. In Zimbabwe, procurement is being supported through the United Nations Development Programme using Global Fund financing.

The company plans to supply the drug to 10 additional African countries in early 2027 and expand availability across other countries covered by its licence, subject to national regulatory approvals and procurement arrangements. It also plans to introduce generic lenacapavir in India in the coming months, subject to regulatory clearance.

• Lenacapavir is used as pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) to reduce the risk of acquiring HIV. Unlike daily oral PrEP medicines, the injectable formulation is administered once every six months.
